articles.title: The 12 Boldest U.S. Open Player Looks That Defied Convention Throughout the Years
articles.summary: They wore what?
articles.body:
Since 1881, the U.S. Open has been one of the most prestigious tennis tournaments of the year.

Players often opt for classic tennis whites, athleisure, or performance-driven ensembles designed for the court.

InStyle looks back at the moments professional athletes refused to play it safe with their on-court style.

Ah , the U.S. Open . Dating all the way back to 1881, the buzzy tennis tournament has become one of the biggest sporting events of the year. Today, the action unfolds at the Arthur Ashe Stadium in Queens. It's also the time where we overuse the term " tenniscore ", break out our preppiest pieces, and hunker down for some seriously good tennis. And of course, the world's best players prepare more than just their game for a tournament like this. Their ensembles have become part of the spectacle, too. While tennis style has long been associated with crisp whites , athleisure, and performance-minded pieces , the U.S. Open has also given players plenty of room to experiment—and some have taken full advantage.

Over the years, a handful of athletes have refused to play it safe, making bold statements with their on- and off-court style. Back in the '90s, when tennis style tended to skew a bit more conservative, Andre Agassi and the Williams sisters weren't afraid to push the style boundaries during their matches. Fast forward to 2025, and Naomi Osaka took the bag charm craze to another level with custom Labubus .

To get in the spirit this year, we're revisiting 12 of the boldest looks to ever hit the U.S. Open.

John McEnroe wasn't afriad to show a little leg at the 1980 U.S. Open. The tennis star took to the court in seriously short shorts paired with a classic polo and his signature headband, creating a look that feels quintessentially '80s today.

Andre Agassi's Mullet and Neon Look (1990)

Andre Agassi brought rebellious energy in 1990, pairing his signature mullet with a bold neon ensemble that stood out against tennis's traditionally preppy aesthetic. With bright colors, denim-inspired details, and plenty of attitude, his look helped usher in a more expressive era of on-court style.

Venus and Serena Williams made their beaded braids a signature part of their early careers, bringing a distinctive sense of personal style to the court. While the beads occasionally sparked debate over the noise they made during play, the look ultimately became an iconic part of the sisters' legacy—and helped broaden perceptions of what a tennis star could look like.

Serena Williams turned heads in 2002 when she stepped out in a skin-tight, black Puma catsuit that looked like more of a fashion statement than traditional tennis attire. Paired with pops of light pink sweat bands, the daring look became one of her most memorable on-court outfits.

Serena Williams brought street style to the court at the 2004 U.S. Open, sporting a Nike denim-look mini skirt paired with a studded black tank and matching accessories. Looking back, the denim, studs, and body-skimming silhouette feel totally Y2K-coded.

Maria Sharapova's Swarovski Crystal Dress (2006)

Maria Sharapova brought some serious sparkle to the 2006 U.S. Open in a black Nike dress embellished with Swarovski crystals. Inspired by New York City at night, the glamorous design was a fitting choice for the tournament's evening matches.

Bethanie Mattek-Sands' Leopard Print (2007)

Bethanie Mattek-Sands went wild at the 2007 U.S. Open, hitting the court in a leopard-print ensemble complete with a matching headband. Known for her unconventional approach to tennis fashion, the American player proved she wasn't afraid to stand out from the competition.

Roger Federer's "Darth Federer" Look (2007)

Roger Federer embraced his dark side in 2007. He stepped onto the court in an all-black Nike ensemble that quickly earned him the nickname "Darth Federer." Complete with black sneakers and a matching headband, the monochromatic look was a sleek departure from traditional tennis whites.

Caroline Wozniacki's Mesh Stella McCartney Dress (2010)

Caroline Wozniacki put a fashion-forward spin on tennis wear in a Stella McCartney for Adidas dress featuring sheer mesh detailing and a super-short silhouette. The unexpected design brought a little edge to the court while still feeling sporty.

Carlos Alcaraz's Sleeveless Basketball Jersey (2023)

Carlos Alcaraz brought a basketball-inspired edge to the 2023 U.S. Open, competing in a sleeveless Nike top that resembled a jersey. Paired with red shorts, the sporty look felt more NBA than country club.

Brat summer carried on at the 2024 U.S. Open, where Naomi Osaka stepped onto the court in a custom Nike look featuring a bright green dress and an oversized bow. Designed in collaboration with Yoon Ahn of AMBUSH, the playful ensemble mixed coquette details with performance tennis wear.

Naomi Osaka's Blinged-Out Labubus (2025)

Naomi Osaka took the Labubu phenomenon courtside (usually attached to her tennis bags) at the 2025 U.S. Open with custom, blinged-out versions of the viral bag charm by New York-based accessories brand A-Morir. Dubbed "Lablingblings," the 3-D printed charms feature approximately 3,000 hand-applied crystals, taking one of 2025's biggest trends to dazzling new heights.

articles.title: ‘Men would never have to face this’: Keyaa Banerji calls out sexism after viral 140kg deadlift and World Championship silver
articles.summary: More sports News: NEW DELHI: Indian powerlifter Keyaa Kunal Banerji had every reason to expect attention after producing one of the standout performances of her young c.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian powerlifter Keyaa Kunal Banerji had every reason to expect attention after producing one of the standout performances of her young career. Instead, the 21-year-old found herself confronting an uncomfortable side of online fame after her 140kg deadlift and World Championship silver medal went viral.Banerji's breakthrough came at the 2026 IPF World Sub-Junior and Junior Classic Powerlifting Championships in Sun City, South Africa, where she competed in the Junior Women's 47kg category. Weighing 45.70kg, she pulled 140kg in the deadlift — more than three times her competition bodyweight — to finish second in the individual deadlift event and win a silver medal.But as the clip of her lift spread across social media, much of the conversation around her achievement shifted away from powerlifting. Banerji said she was subjected to trolling, fake accounts, misuse of her images and thousands of unauthorised AI-generated manipulated images using her likeness.For the young athlete, the experience was not simply about unpleasant comments. She saw it as a stark example of the sexism women athletes continue to encounter when their achievements attract a large online audience.ALSO READ: Keyaa Banerji lifted 140kg and went viral. Then came thousands of AI images, fake accounts and online abuse — why she created a new Instagram account"I think it was just sexism at its finest. I don't think I can put it any other way. The way I was treated - men would never have to face this, like after winning a championship or something like that; a male athlete never has to face something like this," Banerji told ANI."Most of the conversation revolved around my appearance. All people would talk about was my appearance, and I think that really bothered me because I had accomplished something so big for myself and I had done something so big in my sport," she added.A medal, a viral lift and an uncomfortable spotlightThe irony was not lost on Banerji. The lift that drew widespread attention was itself the product of years of work and a sport that she has come to deeply enjoy.At the World Championships, Banerji also recorded a 90kg squat and a 50kg bench press, finishing with a 280kg total and placing fifth overall in the Junior Women's 47kg category. France's Ines Herbaux won the individual deadlift gold with 165kg, while Ireland's Blathnaid O'Dwyer also lifted 140kg.Banerji, however, had arrived at the competition with ambitions that went beyond simply making the podium."I think initially it is a great feeling. Once it came out on social media, I did get a little bit overwhelmed. There was some negative attention, but I would like to avoid talking about that too much. I am very proud of myself and very happy with my accomplishment. I have been working towards this for two years," she said.The silver medal itself had not been part of her original expectations."This silver medal was something I wasn't expecting initially. I was just happy to be present at the World Championship because powerlifting is a long-term sport. I do have plans of eventually winning a World Championship and getting a gold back for the country," Banerji said."It started with me thinking that this World Championship is something I'm going to attend just for experience. The fact that I ended up putting such a good number up and winning a medal was just absolutely incredible," she added.The 140kg deadlift became the defining moment of her campaign, but Banerji's own assessment of the lift was more measured. She explained that competition-day performances can differ considerably from what an athlete manages in training."Competition day numbers and training numbers aren't always the same. Performing as an athlete on competition day is very different from what you do in training. In powerlifting, we usually try to hit maxes in competition," she said."Although my result worked out in a way that I won a silver medal, as an athlete, the planning that my coach and I had done, 140 kg was on the lower end of the range for what we were planning to hit that day," she added.‘I was aiming to break the Asian record’In training, Banerji had already gone beyond that mark."In training, I have hit around 147.5 kg and 150 kg several times. 147.5 kg is also the Asian record. So, my ideal day would have been breaking the Asian record on stage. I was a little disheartened that I wasn't able to do that," she said.The 140kg lift was only her second deadlift attempt. She subsequently went for 142.5kg but could not complete it."140 kg wasn't my third deadlift; it was my second deadlift. It moved a little bit slower than expected compared to how it moves in training. So, I took a smaller jump of 142.5 after that, and I failed that lift. It wasn't an ideal day, but things worked out," she said.‘It’s always something I really enjoyed’While the online attention was difficult, Banerji does not want the trolling to define the story of her World Championship campaign."In fact, I'm really grateful for the opportunity to be talking to news channels because it gives me the opportunity to actually talk about my passion for the sport and my journey progressing my numbers, etc. So, I'm over it. I'm definitely over it. But it was a little bit hard in the middle," she said.That passion dates back to when powerlifting was not even part of her plans."When I was first starting out, I just started going to the gym for a sense of personal fulfilment and just taking care of my health, etc. But I had a friend who was a powerlifting coach and was also competing at a world level. He has also won a gold medal for the country. So, I felt extremely inspired and felt very curious about how this works," she said.That curiosity eventually became competitive ambition as her numbers improved in the squat, bench press and deadlift.More than just lifting heavy weightsBanerji also stressed that powerlifting is a highly technical discipline, contrary to the simplistic perception that it is merely about lifting as much weight as possible."There are rules, making sure that your lift matches the commands of the referee, making sure that once you've picked up, for instance, once you've completed your deadlift, you can't just leave the bar. You can only put it down once the referee asks you to put it down. So, there are a lot of, it's a very technical sport. There are a lot of things that go into it," she said.For Banerji, the sport has also been a constant through an important period of her life."My sport is something that really helped me in my life. During my college times, I used to look forward to training. Sometimes I would have to train at night, sometimes I would have to skip classes to train, but it's something that never really bothered me. It's always something I really enjoyed," she said.Looking beyond the online noiseHer progression is reflected in her numbers. At the 2025 National Championship, she lifted 82.5kg in the squat, 47.5kg in the bench press and 127.5kg in the deadlift for a 257.5kg total. She later improved to 95kg in the squat, 52.5kg in the bench press and 140kg in the deadlift, taking her total to 287.5kg.The World Championship therefore represented another significant step, even if her own assessment suggests there is considerably more to come."I can't explain it, and I am overwhelmed. I was very happy to just be there. To be at that World Championship, meet my competitors, see the girls that I used to look up to around me and compete in the same competition — it was an unreal feeling," she said.Banerji, who recently graduated from Ashoka University with a BSc in Psychology, is considering pursuing an MBA. But her immediate sporting ambition remains clear: continue improving her numbers and eventually win a World Championship gold for India.The unwanted online attention may have become part of her story, but it is not what Banerji wants to be remembered for.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma's Rs.1,300 crore empire: How India's power couple built a business portfolio beyond cricket and Bollywood
articles.summary: Off the field News: Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma have built more than just successful careers in cricket and Bollywood. Together, the couple has created a wide-ranging .
articles.body: Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma have built more than just successful careers in cricket and Bollywood. Together, the couple has created a wide-ranging financial and business portfolio that extends into fashion, hospitality, food-tech, fitness, media, lifestyle and startup investments.Their combined net worth is estimated at more than ₹1,300 crore, according to multiple published reports. While Kohli has developed one of India's biggest athlete-led business portfolios, Sharma has expanded her presence beyond acting through fashion, film production, content and investments in emerging companies.The couple's wealth comes from several sources, including cricket contracts, film assignments, endorsement deals, equity investments, hospitality ventures and consumer brands.Virat Kohli's net worth and earningsVirat Kohli's net worth is estimated to be between ₹1,050 crore and ₹1,115 crore, according to multiple published reports.The former India captain remains one of the country's most commercially valuable sporting personalities, with his income extending well beyond his playing contracts. His earnings come from cricket, endorsements, equity partnerships and businesses associated with his brand.Kohli is reportedly paid ₹21 crore per season by Royal Challengers Bengaluru in the IPL, while his BCCI central contract brings him another ₹3 crore.Endorsements form another major part of his earnings. Reports suggest that Kohli charges between ₹7.5 crore and ₹10 crore for an endorsement deal, helping him remain among India's highest-paid celebrity endorsers.From brand ambassador to businessmanKohli's business journey has evolved significantly over the years. Rather than limiting himself to endorsement deals, he has built and invested in businesses across several sectors.One8 and One8 CommuneOne of Kohli's most prominent ventures is One8, a lifestyle and athleisure brand that has grown into a wider consumer business.The brand has also moved into hospitality through One8 Commune, a premium restaurant and cafe chain with outlets across major Indian metros.WROGNKohli is also associated with WROGN, the youth-focused fashion label operated by Universal Sportsbiz Pvt Ltd (USPL).The brand has established itself in India's casualwear market and remains an important component of Kohli's wider business interests.Kohli's startup investmentsKohli has also put money into several startups and emerging businesses. His investment portfolio includes Blue Tribe Foods, Rage Coffee, Go Digit Insurance, Hyperice, Chisel Fitness, FC Goa, Team Blue Rising Sports and Convo.The range of these investments reflects the areas in which Kohli has increasingly focused his business interests, including wellness, technology, sports and consumer-focused companies.A vast endorsement portfolioKohli's commercial portfolio covers several sectors, including automobiles, banking, technology, fashion and consumer products.Some of the major brands associated with the cricketer include MRF, HSBC India, Myntra, Puma, Noise and Agilitas Sports.Industry reports have consistently placed Kohli among India's highest-paid celebrity endorsers, with his enormous popularity allowing him to command substantial fees from brands.Anushka Sharma's net worthAnushka Sharma has built a sizeable fortune of her own through acting, production, endorsements, fashion and investments.Her net worth is estimated at around ₹255 crore to ₹260 crore, according to published reports.Although Sharma has acted in few films in recent years, with her last theatrical movie being Zero, which was released in December 2018. Her income streams have continued through brand partnerships, digital collaborations, consumer businesses, and investments.Her career has therefore moved beyond the traditional Bollywood model, with business ventures becoming an increasingly important part of her financial portfolio.Nush: Sharma's fashion ventureOne of Anushka Sharma's most visible businesses is Nush, her fashion and lifestyle label.Founded in 2017, Nush focuses on affordable everyday clothing and is available through major online marketplaces.The brand has given Sharma a presence in the consumer fashion space while complementing her work as an actor and public figure.Clean Slate FilmzSharma also entered film production with her brother Karnesh Sharma when the two co-founded Clean Slate Filmz in 2013.The production company backed several notable projects, including NH10, Pari, Bulbbul, Paatal Lok, Qala and Kohrra.Sharma stepped away from the company's operational responsibilities in 2022, after which Karnesh Sharma continued to lead the business.The production house remains an important part of the couple's wider connection with India's entertainment industry, even as Sharma has reduced her involvement in its day-to-day operations.Anushka Sharma's startup investmentsLike Kohli, Sharma has also invested in new-age businesses.Her investment portfolio includes consumer-focused companies such as Slurrp Farm and Blue Tribe Foods.Her choices have largely centred on areas such as health, sustainability and lifestyle, giving her exposure to sectors beyond the entertainment industry.Endorsement dealsSharma has also maintained a strong commercial presence through endorsement partnerships.Her brand portfolio has covered beauty, fashion, jewellery and banking, with companies such as Myntra, Nivea, Garnier, Tanishq, Puma, Lavie and Pantene among the brands associated with her.These partnerships have helped Sharma remain one of India's most sought-after celebrity endorsers despite appearing in fewer films in recent years.Luxury real estate adds to their wealthThe couple's business interests are complemented by a substantial luxury property portfolio.Reports suggest Kohli owns prime properties in Gurugram, Mumbai and Alibaug, while Sharma also has significant residential investments.Their combined real estate holdings are estimated to be worth more than ₹100 crore, adding another major asset class to their overall wealth.Kohli and Sharma's latest property purchaseThe couple recently added another high-value asset to their portfolio by purchasing a 2,644 sq ft apartment in Mumbai's Versova neighbourhood.The property was bought for ₹18.29 crore and forms part of a premium residential development.The purchase further underlines the couple's continuing interest in high-value real estate alongside their investments in consumer businesses, hospitality and startups.How the ₹1,300 crore-plus empire comes togetherKohli and Sharma's combined wealth is not dependent on a single source of income.Kohli's cricket earnings and enormous endorsement portfolio sit alongside his investments in sports, fashion, food-tech, fitness and technology. Sharma, meanwhile, has built income streams through acting, production, fashion, endorsements and startup investments.Their business interests therefore stretch across several industries rather than being concentrated solely on their respective careers.With their combined net worth estimated at more than ₹1,300 crore, Kohli and Sharma have developed one of India's most diversified celebrity business portfolios.And Kohli's cricket career continues to add another layer to that financial picture.Virat Kohli set for India returnKohli will be back in action for India on September 27, when India take on the West Indies in a three-match ODI series.The veteran batter now plays only ODI cricket for India after retiring from both Test and T20I cricket.He has been in strong form in 2026, scoring 384 runs in six ODIs at an average of 64.00. His tally includes three fifties and one century, with a best score of 124.Kohli also played a major role in Royal Challengers Bengaluru successfully defending their IPL trophy in 2026.He scored 675 runs in 16 innings at an average of 56.25 and a strike rate of 165.85. The campaign also saw him register his fastest IPL half-century, reaching the landmark in 25 balls in the final.Kohli was named Player of the Match for his performance in the title clash.With his businesses continuing to expand and his cricket career still generating significant commercial value, Kohli's financial empire remains closely tied to both his sporting success and his ability to build brands beyond the cricket field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The America-Russia Paradox: One chases historic gold at Chess Olympiad, the other not allowed to play
articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: For most of the 20th century, the Chess Olympiad was one of the few arenas where the Cold War actually played out on a board. The Soviet Un.
articles.body: BENGALURU: For most of the 20th century, the Chess Olympiad was one of the few arenas where the Cold War actually played out on a board. The Soviet Union treated the biennial team event as a matter of state prestige, fielding lineups stacked with world champions and winning eighteen gold medals between 1952 and 1990.The United States, briefly dominant in the 1930s behind Frank Marshall's golden generation, spent the second half of the century chasing that shadow. They came closest in 1976, winning a gold only because the Soviets and their Eastern Bloc allies boycotted the tournament in Haifa, Israel, over FIDE's refusal to move the venue. Bobby Fischer's defeat of Boris Spassky in Reykjavik in 1972 remains the sport's most mythologised individual clash, but the Olympiad was always the collective version of the same rivalry.Fifty years on, the framing has flipped entirely. Russia inherited the Soviet Union's chess machinery after 1991 and kept winning through the 2000s, eventually matching the United States with six Olympiad golds apiece.But as the 46th Chess Olympiad approaches in Samarkand from September 15–27, it is the United States sending a stacked five-man roster chasing team glory, and Russia, for a third consecutive cycle, will not be able to send anyone at all.Levon Aronian will play for Team USA this September, alongside Fabiano Caruana, Wesley So, Hans Niemann and Awonder Liang, with IM John Donaldson captaining and GM Grigory Oparin as trainer.It will be Aronian's third Olympiad since he switched from Armenia, a country for which he won gold as part of three separate Olympiad-winning teams, to the United States in late 2021. He debuted for the US in Chennai in 2022, won team silver on board four in Budapest in 2024, and now arrives in Samarkand with an unusually specific ambition."I was thinking that it would be a good time to win an Olympiad because I don't know if there are many people who have won four Olympiads," Aronian told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction. "I haven't checked. I would like to join that club."Asked which teams stood in the way beyond the obvious contenders besides India, Aronian didn't hesitate to name a few."It's going to be tough against Uzbekistan. I also think China can be very strong; they always have underrated players," the veteran Grandmaster opined. "Traditionally, Armenia can play well, and this time, I think Germany is also a good team."Currently playing for Ganges Grandmasters at the Global Chess League (GCL), he feels the league could be a useful rehearsal for exactly the kind of pressure he will be facing at the Chess Olympiad."There's always tension in this tournament. Teams want to play well. It's good to simulate that situation where everything depends on you. It always happens," the 43-year-old Grandmaster added.On the other hand, though, there will be no equivalent build-up for Ian Nepomniachtchi. The current Russian No. 1 and a two-time World Championship challenger will not be in Samarkand, after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ordered FIDE to suspend the Russian Chess Federation following a complaint from Ukraine's federation over tournaments staged in occupied territory.FIDE's Council complied only partially with the ruling, prompting protests from several national federations. The politics reached the top of the sport itself in July, when FIDE president Arkady Dvorkovich, a former Russian deputy prime minister, voluntarily stepped aside from his duties after being added to the European Union's sanctions list."It's very unfortunate," the 36-year-old Russian Grandmaster told this website exclusively on the sidelines of GCL. "What makes it even worse is that we had very high hopes. Russian sport is getting back this year, with a lot of teams in other sports participating in World Championships. We would expect chess to be one of those too."But maybe the fact that Dvorkovich got onto the sanctions list early this summer brought some changes. There was also the unfortunate CAS case, which didn't go well for the Russian Chess Federation. Even after that, we expected Russia to participate, maybe in neutral status," Nepo added. However, the wish to play under a neutral flag has not been granted.Not being too critical of the situation, he just hopes that everything gets sorted out for the sake of the sport. "Belarus is playing, and Russia is not. Hopefully things will get better; for sport, and not just for sport," the Ganges Grandmaster icon player remarked.Set side by side, the two situations barely resemble the same sport.One player is refining a personal record, treating a franchise league as a dress rehearsal for a tournament he expects to win.Also Read: 8 months, Moscow-to-Munich flights, but now he is 'fed up': Behind Russia No. 1 Ian Nepomniachtchi's tattoosThe other is watching a competition happen without him, for reasons that have nothing to do with how he plays chess.It's a reminder that the Olympiad, for all its history as a proxy battlefield between Washington and Moscow, was at least always a battlefield both sides got to enter. In Samarkand this year, just like the previous two editions, only one of them will.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL Power Rankings: Are the Bills and Josh Allen the biggest threat to the Rams' reign?
articles.summary: The Bills come into the season as one of the AFC's strongest teams.
articles.body:
NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

It's going to take something special to knock off the Los Angeles Rams this season. Perhaps the current titleholder of best quarterback in football.

The Rams are clearly the Super Bowl favorite . That doesn't mean they're guaranteed to win a championship (in fact, every recent favorite as strong as the Rams have failed in that mission). There are plenty of teams capable of beating the Rams in a one-and-done playoff format.

The Seahawks are the obvious pick to oust the Rams, considering they beat them two of three times last season and won a Super Bowl. Seattle was a dominant champion , and while there have been some changes, the foundation remains. But perhaps it's finally time for one of the NFL's best players to get a championship ring.

The Buffalo Bills displayed some urgency to get Josh Allen to a Super Bowl, firing Sean McDermott after an overtime loss in the divisional round of the playoffs. They hired Joe Brady as their new head coach, traded for receiver DJ Moore and made some improvements to the defense in chase of a championship. Allen turned 30 in May, which isn't ancient for a quarterback. But there won't be infinite opportunities with him either.

Allen has had some monster games against the Rams, if that ends up being a Super Bowl matchup. In three outings against the Rams, he has 950 passing yards and 10 touchdowns with 146 rushing yards and five more touchdowns on the ground. His average against the Rams is more than 300 yards passing, almost 50 yards rushing and five total touchdowns. Those Los Angeles defenses didn't have Myles Garrett, but Allen has torched Sean McVay's teams before.

We'll see the matchup in Week 5, when the Bills play at the Rams on a Monday night. Maybe we'll get a rematch in Super Bowl LXI, which will also be at SoFi Stadium. It'll take a memorable performance to beat the Rams this season. Allen has that type of historic game in him.

Here are the power rankings before Week 1 (in this edition, last week's rankings is from our offseason countdown ):

The Dolphins claimed seven players off waivers. The fact that 13% of their roster is made up of players who weren't wanted by other teams and didn't go through training camp with the Dolphins tells you all you need to know about Miami's upcoming season. It's going to be ugly.

The most egregious injury of the preseason was running back Jeremiyah Love, the third overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft who suffered a high ankle sprain as he got 14 first-half touches in his preseason debut. If Love is affected for most or some of his rookie season — high ankle sprains can linger for a while — it's not a good look for rookie head coach Mike LaFleur.

Everything has been said about Deshaun Watson starting at quarterback. It's a weird, bad decision. That detracts from the exciting young talent on the rest of the team. Keep a close eye on rookie receiver KC Concepcion, a first-round draft pick who will contribute a lot right away.

Geno Smith threw seven preseason passes. He completed all seven for 65 yards and a touchdown. One drive in the preseason shouldn't change perceptions that much, but it's a reminder that not long ago Smith was a competent starter in Seattle.

The Falcons' quarterback situation isn't good. Just as bad is that they drafted two edge rushers in the first round last season, and Jalon Walker is out for the season with a torn ACL and James Pearce Jr. is suspended for the first eight games. It's hard to get too excited for this Atlanta season.

Cam Ward completed 13 of 24 passes for 126 yards in the preseason and struggled on any downfield throws. Some have fairly pointed out that he was better in joint practices. We're going to get to see. Ward faces a huge season in his career path.

The Raiders are going with Kirk Cousins to start the season and he gets an advantageous matchup right away, against a Dolphins team that's dead last in these rankings. Don't forget the Raiders won in Week 1 last season, getting a confounding road win over a Patriots team that went 14-2 the rest of the season.

The Panthers will be without both starting tackles early in the season, and that doesn't help a team that already had some regression tendencies . They'll need to figure out a way to score points in Week 1 against a fun Bears offense.

The Saints are a trendy pick to win the NFC South, but training camp injuries to receiver Jordyn Tyson and defensive lineman Bryan Bresee are huge losses on each side of the ball. The Saints could still win a bad division, but the path is a lot tougher without those two standouts.

Malik Nabers' availability for the start of the season has been a hot topic for weeks, but the fact that he has come along pretty well is good news overall. If Nabers can play most of the season at his normal level, it raises the Giants' ceiling.

No preseason injury was more damaging than the Commanders losing left tackle Laremy Tunsil for all or most of the season. That will affect the entire offense, which didn't add much in the offseason . This is not how Jayden Daniels wanted to start his third season.

The mystery surrounding Emeka Egbuka's toe injury makes it tough to rank the Buccaneers. Egbuka is clearly the Buccaneers' alpha receiver if healthy, but if he has a turf toe injury, that could affect him for a while. He didn't play well last season after taking on some injuries. Now without Mike Evans, the Buccaneers need Egbuka to break out.

The Steelers and Falcons were tied for the oldest roster in the NFL after the cutdown to 53 players, according to Spotrac . That's truly bad for the Falcons, who are nowhere near contention, but it's not good for the Steelers either. Pittsburgh keeps chasing a low ceiling , especially through its commitment to 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers. It's a curious plan.

We didn't see Daniel Jones through the preseason, but reports from training camp and preseason have been positive as he comes back from a torn Achilles. The Colts scored just short of 30 points a game in the 12 games before Jones' injury, and 21.8 in the final five games of the season.

In 2021, Kyler Murray had a solid season with a 100.6 passer rating. Since then he hasn't posted a rating above 93.5 and his overall rating over four seasons is a mediocre 90.3. In other words, it has been a while since Murray was a plus quarterback. Maybe he improves in Kevin O'Connell's scheme. At very least he'll be better than the Vikings' options last season.

Josh Jacobs landing on the commissioner's exempt list affects the Packers' season, since they don't know if or when he'll play. MarShawn Lloyd is talented but he has six carries over two seasons due to injuries. There isn't much behind him. This should force the Packers to pass more with Jordan Love, which might not be a bad thing. Love was second in the NFL in adjusted EPA ( expected points added ) per play last season and maybe can turn that efficiency into a huge season.

One of the quieter injury stories through August was defensive end Nick Bosa missing most of camp. He has knee tendinitis after tearing his ACL last season. The 49ers face a big challenge against the Rams in Australia, and it doesn't get easier if Bosa and George Kittle are limited coming off injuries.

The Bengals are a conundrum. Their offense should be fantastic, if the line holds up, but how much better will their defense be? They were 30th in defensive DVOA last season and while Dexter Lawrence II and other additions will help, they also lost Trey Hendrickson and have a long way to go to be average. Also keep in mind: The Bengals are notoriously slow starters under head coach Zac Taylor. They haven't gotten out of September with a winning record since 2021.

The Jaguars have an easy start to the season, with a home game against the Browns. They better win. After that they have: at Denver, vs. Patriots, at Bengals, vs. Eagles, vs. Texans. It wouldn't be bad for the Jaguars to get out of that stretch at 3-3, but that is unlikely if they drop a game to Cleveland in Week 1.

The Chargers lost center Tyler Biadasz to a season-ending injury, turning the interior of the offensive line into a big question mark. The AFC West is competitive enough that an injury like that could be a big factor in the race.

Patrick Mahomes is likely going to start in Week 1 coming off an ACL surgery, but it will be a bit of an unusual Week 1 for him. Mahomes and the rest of the Chiefs' starters usually log some time in the preseason. Mahomes didn't play at all this preseason as the Chiefs played it safe with him. However, in 2020, when there were no preseason games due to the pandemic, Mahomes had 11 touchdowns and no interceptions in his first four games. We'll see if he looks rusty early this season.

Ben Johnson has stated he wants to field the highest scoring offense in NFL history. That mark was set by the 2013 Broncos, who averaged 37.9 points. That would be a massive leap from the 25.9 points per game the Bears scored last season. There's nothing wrong with lofty goals, and if Caleb Williams makes the leap to being an MVP candidate, Chicago could at least make a run at the highest scoring offense in the NFL this season.

The Texans were lucky to replace injured Jayden Higgins with Kayshon Boutte. Apparently there was no trade market for Boutte, whom the Texans got from the Patriots for a 2028 seventh-round pick. Boutte had 551 yards and six touchdowns last season and will have a role in the offense.

The Lions traded David Montgomery and might regret it. Isiah Pacheco is on injured reserve with general manager Brad Holmes saying he is "hopeful" Pacheco returns this season. The current backups are Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki. They have a combined nine carries for 29 yards in the NFL. The Lions desperately need Jahmyr Gibbs to stay healthy. They are also very thin in the secondary to start the season.

The Eagles were under center for about 35% of their training camp snaps, according to PhillyVoice.com , which is a big change for Jalen Hurts. The Eagles were at 21.8% snaps under center and 15.6% in 2024, PhillyVoice.com said. The change to offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, who has never called plays in the NFL, and a much different scheme makes the Eagles tough to project going into the season.

Dallas' offense hasn't been a question all offseason. Everyone assumes it will be very good. It should be, unless running back Javonte Williams misses time or has his play dip. There is practically nothing behind him. Backup Malik Davis has 90 career carries, and 38 of them came in 2022. The depth at running back is worth keeping an eye on.

Tyler Loop was pretty good as a rookie last season. He hit 30-of-34 field-goal attempts, though he wasn't great from beyond 50 yards. But he had a memorable miss to end the season, which kept the Ravens from making the playoffs, then had some misses in the preseason. The Ravens signed Jake Moody to the practice squad, a clear sign that if Loop struggles early, he won't keep the job.

Even though the Patriots drafted left tackle Caleb Lomu in the first round of the NFL Draft, last year's first-round pick, Will Campbell, has remained with the first team at left tackle. Campbell was picked apart after a rough postseason, including a bad Super Bowl. A knee injury in November might be to blame. He'll start the season at left tackle but we'll see how long his leash is if he struggles.

The Broncos didn't have a first-round pick because they traded for Jaylen Waddle, but perhaps they found an immediate contributor in the fourth round with running back Jonah Coleman. All of the reports on Coleman have been positive, and that's valuable considering J.K. Dobbins' injury history. Coleman could be an important player for a very good team.

The biggest news of August for the Bills was that tight end Dalton Kincaid was healthy. Injuries have cost Kincaid eight games over the past two seasons. Kincaid had a scorching 2.7 yards per route run last season, a fantastic mark for a tight end. Now he just needs to stay on the field to run more routes with Josh Allen.

A lot of the Seahawks' season depends on first-round pick Jadarian Price replacing Kenneth Walker III. Seattle led the NFL last season with a 48% rush rate, which is a product of winning a lot of games but also part of their philosophy. Zach Charbonnet is out the first four weeks as he recovers from an ACL injury, so the runway is clear for Price to take off early.

Not much more can be said about the Rams. No disrespect to the Seahawks, but there's no question who should be No. 1 going into the season. This is one of the most loaded rosters you'll find , even if that doesn't guarantee a Super Bowl .

articles.title: Eddie Hearn shuts down Tyson Fury’s claims of Anthony Joshua “Pulling Out” of their fight as Gypsy King’s “Joshua has s**t his pants” Instagram video goes viral

articles.body: Anthony Joshua has not pulled out of his planned fight with Tyson Fury, according to his long-time promoter Eddie Hearn. Hearn has insisted that the two former heavyweight world champions still have a legally binding agreement to face each other this year.The fight is facing a major problem over its location. Joshua’s contract requires the bout to take place in the UK, while Netflix and Saudi boxing financier Turki Alalshikh are pushing for the event to be held in the United States. Wembley remains a possible option.Eddie Hearn insists Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight is still onEddie Hearn has rejected claims that Anthony Joshua has walked away from the highly anticipated fight with Tyson Fury.Fury claimed on Instagram that Joshua had “s**t his pants” and suggested that their long-awaited Battle of Britain fight was off. The former WBC heavyweight champion then called out Oleksandr Usyk for a possible trilogy fight. However, Hearn has strongly denied that Joshua has withdrawn from the contest.Speaking to SunSport, Joshua’s promoter said, “We have a signed legally binding contract to fight Tyson Fury and that’s exactly what we will be doing.”The main issue is not the fight itself but where it will take place. Joshua’s agreement, which was signed in April, reportedly states that the fight must happen in the UK. However, Netflix and Saudi boxing financier Turki Alalshikh are keen to stage the blockbuster event in America.New York’s Madison Square Garden has emerged as the leading option. The venue could help the fight reach a bigger American television audience. However, there has been a fresh push to bring the fight back to Britain.Wembley Stadium is now being discussed as a possible venue. Hearn has been publicly calling for the fight to be staged in the UK. He believes Joshua wants the event to happen in front of British fans.Hearn has also revealed that he is set to speak with London Mayor Sadiq Khan as efforts continue to make Wembley a realistic option.Speaking in Dublin, Hearn said, “Thank you to all the people that have supported it because you’ve got the attention of (promoters) Sela. And those talks now are really heating up and moving quickly about a possible Wembley fight.”A Wembley fight could require a much later start time. The bout may begin around 2am in the UK to suit American viewers.Meanwhile, Fury is currently training in Miami. He has turned his attention towards Usyk after claiming the Joshua fight was off. Fury and Usyk have already fought twice, with the Ukrainian winning both encounters in 2024.For now, Hearn’s message is clear, Joshua has not pulled out, and negotiations are continuing to try to bring Fury vs Joshua to Britain.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Liam Farrell: Wigan Warriors captain on retirement, fond memories, and next steps after Super League career to remember
articles.summary: Liam Farrell joined Sky Sports' The Bench podcast to discuss his decision to retire, what comes next, and if we will see him in a Wigan Warriors shirt again; The regular Super League season concludes with Round 27 from Thursday September 10 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The 36-year-old, who has only ever played for the Warriors, will call time on a career which has spanned 17 professional seasons. Farrell has captained Wigan since 2023 and been capped 12 times by England.

He has totalled 428 appearances for Wigan and scored 151 tries, winning six Super League titles, five Challenge Cups and two World Club Challenge successes during his illustrious career.

Farrell has not featured since June with an ongoing neck issue and with just three potential matches remaining in the season for his club, the chances of him featuring again for his boyhood club are in doubt.

That third match, if Wigan were to make it, would be the Super League Grand Final at Old Trafford on October 3, live on Sky Sports .

Of course, it would be a dream for Farrell to lead his team out once again at the Theatre of Dreams, but he remains aware that not every career concludes with a fairy-tale ending.

"It is one of them - who knows," Farrell told Sky Sports' The Bench podcast.

"I have still got to see the specialist again and see what he recommends and there will be a decision made in the near future.

"That is all I have got for now. Careers don't always end how you want them to end.

"Don't get me wrong, I would love it to end that way, but I'll wait and see what the next few weeks bring.

"Regardless of how it does end up, I have done more than I ever wanted to achieve and I would be happy whichever way it goes.

"I am at peace with that. It would have been nice to maybe just play one more game but like I said, things don't always finish the way you want them to.

"We will just wait and see what the decision is in the next few weeks."

While time will tell on whether we will see Farrell in a Wigan jersey one more time, he remains adamant that pulling on the cherry and white just once would have been enough.

"I have lived a lot of my dreams. I think one thing I said to the lads over there: my goal was always one game for Wigan. If I'd have come off the bench, played once, I'd have been happy and retired there," he added.

"But to have had the career I have had and the success I have had. The teams I have been involved in, the trophies I have won, I have been unbelievably lucky. It is a dream come true for myself."

Joining the 'performance side' of things

While this season marks the end of Farrell's involvement at Wigan as a player, he will now move over to the performance setup, a job he has been working towards in the background for a number of years.

"I got all my qualifications for that a few years ago," Farrell said. "So, that has just been in the back pocket for when the time came of retiring. It is something I'm excited about.

"It is something I want to get into and slowly build into it as well."

The regular Super League season concludes with Round 27 from Thursday September 10 live on Sky Sports.

articles.title: Trial opens in Paris over murder of Argentina rugby star Federico Aramburu
articles.summary: Two ⁠former members of a violent far-right group will face trial on murder and attempted murder charges.
articles.body:
The trial over the murder of former Argentina rugby international ⁠Federico Aramburu opens in ⁠Paris on Monday, more than four years after he was shot dead in the French capital following an altercation near the Boulevard Saint-Germain.

Two ⁠former members of a violent far-right group will face trial on murder and attempted murder charges.

Loik Le Priol, 32, who investigators say fired the fatal shots, ⁠is charged with murder. His associate Romain Bouvier, 35, who prosecutors say also fired a weapon during the incident, is charged with attempted murder.

Both men are already serving prison sentences for aggravated assault in a separate case.

According to the investigation, Aramburu, 42, was having a late drink with friend and fellow former rugby player Shaun Hegarty on the terrace of the Mabillon cafe on March 19, 2022. Le Priol, Bouvier and Le Priol’s then girlfriend, Lyson Rochemir, 29, who is also on trial on an attempted murder charge, were at a nearby table.

Investigators say an altercation broke out between the two groups. CCTV ⁠footage reviewed during the investigation showed a confrontation involving Hegarty ⁠and Le Priol. The dispute escalated into a physical fight involving Aramburu, Hegarty, Le Priol and Bouvier before security staff intervened, according to court documents.

Prosecutors say the confrontation continued outside shortly afterwards. According to ⁠investigators, Bouvier, who had arrived in a car driven by Rochemir, fired shots at Aramburu before Le Priol opened fire. Aramburu ⁠died at the scene.

The three defendants fled, according to prosecutors. ⁠Rochemir was arrested in Paris later that day, and Bouvier a few days later in the Sarthe region. A third man, Antony Sorrentino, is also on trial, accused of helping Bouvier evade arrest. Le Priol was ‌arrested in Hungary while attempting to cross into Ukraine.

The trial is expected to run until September 25, when the court is due to deliver its verdict. ‌Le ‌Priol, Bouvier and Rochemir all face life sentences.

Aramburu won 22 caps for Argentina and played for French clubs including Biarritz and Perpignan.

The trial has prompted calls for justice in Aramburu’s native Argentina, where he played for the national team, with members of the Pumas wearing black T-shirts bearing the words “Justice for Fede” ahead of a match on Saturday.

Former friends and teammates have remembered Aramburu as “always smiling” and a “true friend”, while his loved ones have urged against any attempt to minimise his death.

A campaign backed by his family, friends and the Argentinian rugby community aims to ensure “society remembers what is about to be tried: the murder of a 42-year-old man, father of three children, whose life was snatched away”.

The killing was “marked by violence, hatred and extremist intolerance”, they said.

The Argentine Rugby Union also issued a statement expressing “its support for the call for justice” for Aramburu.

articles.title: Early WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Match Card Predictions After SNME Results
articles.summary: On the heels of the first-ever Sunday Night's Main Event, the attention of the WWE Universe turns toward the annual Money in the Bank premium live event, held this year in New Orleans on October 10.
articles.body:
On the heels of the first-ever Sunday Night's Main Event, the attention of the WWE Universe turns toward the annual Money in the Bank premium live event, held this year in New Orleans on October 10.

Based on the outcome of the Peacock presentation, here are a few matches to consider for the upcoming extravaganza.

Men's Money in the Bank Ladder Match for the Undisputed WWE Championship

What better way to spice up Money in the Bank than by taking the Superstars currently feuding over the Undisputed WWE Championship, adding a ladder and giving fans a historic first?

CM Punk has seen his title reign targeted by Sami Zayn, Kevin Owens, Finn Balor and Gunther in recent weeks. Rather than a convoluted scramble match or a far less entertaining Fatal 5-Way, what better way to bring prestige to the event than by booking a match in which the title is the ultimate prize?

Sure, that shortchanges the men, but an even bigger prize awaits the Superstar who climbs the ladder and retrieves the title.

There are plenty of contenders who could take up places in the women's ladder match.

Stephanie Vaquer, Becky Lynch, Roxanne Perez, Raquel Rodriguez, Sol Ruca and Lyra Valkyria are a few options, and that is just the Raw side of things.

Throw in Charlotte Flair, Jade Cargill, Tiffany Stratton, a Fatal Influence member and newcomer Tatum Paxley, and you have the potential for one of the most loaded fields in event history.

With their never-ending feud, Flair and Cargill feel like shoo-ins, as does Vaquer, especially if she fails to dethrone Morgan on Monday night's Raw.

United States Championship: Trick Williams vs. Carmelo Hayes

This is probably wishful thinking, but can we please get back to Carmelo Hayes challenging for a United States Championship he never should have lost ahead of WrestleMania 42?

A proper feud with Trick Williams over the title, without interruption or the inclusion of another competitor, is just what the former NXT champion needs to heat back up after falling back into obscurity.

The question is where that leaves Baron Corbin, who was excellent at Sunday Night's Main Event, and is unlikely to suddenly wander aimlessly entering the fall months.

Women's World Championship: Becky Lynch vs. Liv Morgan

Assuming that someone of stature is going to miss out on the women's ladder match, Becky Lynch challenging Liv Morgan bolsters the star power of the show and gives the women's division another high-profile matchup.

It is also a relatively fresh contest for the show, with their last encounter occurring inside a steel cage on the May 27, 2024 episode of Raw.

That it could also serve as the latest chapter in the three-way rivalry also involving Vaquer makes it an intriguing option for Money in the Bank.

World Heavyweight Championship: LA Knight vs. Roman Reigns

LA Knight has been calling out Roman Reigns for months in search of a world title match. It feels like he is closer than ever to getting it, with a showdown in New Orleans being a great choice of location.

It is another contest to bolster a card that lives and breathes on the strength of the ladder matches anyway, so it could even get away with a screwy finish that sets up another, more important battle down the line.

Knight has earned the opportunity to rise to the occasion against the top star in the company.

articles.title: Ollie Millroy’s wife Fern Millroy gives graphic update on British racing driver from hospital after his Ferrari’s horror crash during China GT race
articles.summary: International Sports News: British racing driver Ollie Millroy remains in hospital in Shanghai after suffering serious injuries in a horror crash during a China GT event. His wi.
articles.body: British racing driver Ollie Millroy remains in hospital in Shanghai after suffering serious injuries in a horror crash during a China GT event. His wife, Fern Millroy, has now revealed the extent of his injuries following surgery.Fern said the operation went well but revealed that Ollie still needs high-flow oxygen as his lung recovers. She also admitted she “can’t believe” he survived the terrifying incident, while praising fellow driver Loek Hartog for helping pull him from the burning Ferrari.Fern Millroy reveals Ollie Millroy’s injuries after terrifying fireball crashOllie Millroy was involved in a horrific accident at the Shanghai International Circuit during a China GT race. His Ferrari was hit after two other cars collided and spun across the track.The impact caused Ollie’s car to instantly burst into flames. He became trapped inside the Ferrari as the vehicle was engulfed by fire.Loek Hartog, who was also competing in the event, immediately rushed to help. New footage shows the 23-year-old driver desperately searching through the remains of the Ferrari to free Millroy.Ollie later underwent surgery at a hospital in Shanghai.His wife Fern has remained by his side throughout the ordeal. She provided a detailed update on his condition after the operation.She wrote on her Instagram stories, “Surgery went well yesterday, it took several hours, main work being his right hand. He now has metal along the entirety of his clavicle right side, metal inside his right hand, six broken ribs supported with a compression wrap and on high flow oxygen whilst his lung recovers.“Tried to come off the oxygen but his O2 level was just too low. He is in great care at this fantastic hospital in Shanghai and we can’t thank the staff here enough. More X Rays and CT tomorrow morning”, she continued.Fern also highlighted the crucial role played by Hartog. She added, “I still can’t believe he’s alive, purely down to our real life superhero Loek Hartog.”Loek Hartog has also spoken about the support surrounding the incident. He thanked people for their messages before travelling back home.He wrote, “Overwhelmed by the support from everyone over the past two days. I feel incredibly lucky to be part of a racing community that looks after each other the way this one does.”He also thanked everyone for all the messages and support that fans sent to Ollie, his wife and family, and also to him and his family. He revealed that he’s travelling back home now and can’t wait to be there. He also mentioned that he’s feeling good for now, but there have naturally been a lot of thoughts running through his head over the past few days.Notably, Fern and Ollie have been married since 2021 and have three young children. The family is now supporting Ollie as he continues his recovery in hospital.The racing community has also offered support to the British driver and Hartog following the frightening crash.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. This life pivot story has quite the ending – Richard emails: Joe love the column. First time long time. I was a young lawyer at my father’s law firm in 1997. My wife was 7 months pregnant with our first child I worked primarily for a partner in a 2 lawyer Satelite office who generated a lot of work for the firm and was my dad’s protege. She was going on vacation to Aspen. She told me if X(another lawyer from a different firm) comes to the office and asks for a particular client file give it to her. So X did come to the office and I gave her the file. When my boss returned from Aspen I popped my head into her office and asked how was your vacation? She was crying. I said what wrong? She said why did you give X the file? I said because that is what you said to do. She said no I didn’t. I said yes you did and you showed me where the file was. She said she didn’t. So I said well I guess you are calling me a liar. She said yes I am. I said well "F**k you I’m not a liar" and this was in front of her sycophant staff. The partner told my father it was her or me who had to go. My dad backed her so I quit and went home and told my wife I just quit. Started my own firm as a solo which is now a 5 office mid size firm and far far more successful than my former boss and even my father. My dad and I made amends. articles.title: How St Helens let Super League success become long-term stagnation - the flap of a wing!
articles.summary: Sky Sports' Megan Wellens dissects how St Helens succumbed to their worst-ever Super League finish in 2026; the regular Betfred Super League season concludes with Round 27 from Thursday September 10 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The analytical dissection of how this happened has been ongoing by fans and pundits for the best part of two years. Some supporters would say longer.

The next 12 months will give an indication of how long those with power inside the four walls of the club have realised that their trajectory has been downwards.

The famous question posed by meteorologist Edward Lorenz back in the 1970s was 'can the flap of a butterfly's wing in Brazil set off a tornado in Texas?'

Can the smallest of changes lead to significant outcomes in the most complex of systems?

If this low ebb for Saints is their tornado, what exactly was the flap of the wing? What exactly caused the chaos?

For that, we need to rewind to 2019, when they picked up their first Super League title in five years.

2019: The start of a run like never before

Midway through 2017, St Helens were sitting mid-table and made the decision to part ways with head coach Keiron Cunningham and bring in Justin Holbrook.

After a Luke Gale drop goal saw Saints heartbreakingly fall in the semi-finals in 2017 and somehow miss out in 2018 despite the genius of Ben Barba, 2019 marked the year when they were simply the best team around.

The Saints obliterated the competition in 2019, losing just three matches and cantering to the top of the league.

Their 23-6 win over Salford Red Devils in the Grand Final was the moment that cemented that St Helens were here once again.

It was a star-studded team with the likes of Jonny Lomax, Tommy Makinson, Alex Walmsley and Lachlan Coote all in their mid-to-late 20s and in their prime. A mix of homegrown talent and hand-picked Australian superstars was running the show.

They had to then overcome a change of head coach but, under Kristian Woolf, success would continue...

2020-2023: Four in a row leads to climbing Everest

Woolf has spoken openly about the fact that the season shutting down due to Covid potentially saved his job.

Woolf's team had just lost to Huddersfield Giants and Castleford Tigers when the season went on hiatus.

By the time it returned, he had spoken with his playing group about what more they wanted from him and how they wanted things to run. A collaboration between a stern coach and a group striving for success - and continuing to achieve it - was born.

Jack Welsby scored one of the best Grand Final tries ever seen in 2020 and then two more Super League wins followed. Not only that, they won a Challenge Cup and a League Leaders' Shield.

When St Helens headed down under for the World Club Challenge in 2023, no one believed they could beat Penrith Panthers.

Hometown head coach Paul Wellens moved from captain and player to assistant coach, and after over 10 years in the coaching game at the club, he had stepped up to the top job.

Then, Lewis Dodd sent over a golden-point drop goal that is lauded as one of the most seismic moments in the sport in this country.

They had climbed to the top of Everest and planted the St Helens flag.

You have won it all, your players have provided every success you have asked for.

So what is the next task? Is it starting a transition period? Is it trusting this same group of players to provide once again? Is it a mix of both?

Big players were winning big and getting their reward, deservedly so. But in a salary-capped sport, there comes a time where that may start to bite.

By this point, the likes of Makinson, Lomax, Walmsley, Mark Percival, Louis McCarthy-Scarsbrook and Sione Mata'utia had brought unprecedented success. They were also now mostly in their 30s.

Naturally, with that, comes upgraded contracts. Simply put - you win more you deserve to earn more.

But, if contracts are being upgraded year on year, the space on a salary cap dwindles. Your chance to bring in big names dwindles. Your room for youngsters to be earning well dwindles.

A sum of £2.1m only stretches so far and you need to be ruthlessly pragmatic. Or players need to be willing to earn less than what they were receiving in their 20s. A tough sell!

Over the next three seasons under Wellens, St Helens would make just 11 signings to replace the likes of Regan Grace, James Roby, Will Hopoate, Makinson, Lewis Dodd and Mata'utia.

Those signings were Tee Ritson, Wesley Bruines, Daryl Clark, Waqa Blake, Kyle Feldt, Tristan Sailor, Lewis Murphy, Moses Mbye, Matt Whitley, Shane Wright and Deon Cross.

Wright and Cross only became available due to the financial collapse of Salford Red Devils.

Some would argue those big boots have still not been filled. Or if they have been filled, the successor has not matched up to their predecessor.

Back in 2025, former St Helens CEO Mike Rush described the club's recruitment strategy as 'Moneyball'.

Moneyball is a term coined from Michael Lewis' book which analysed how, in 2002, Oakland Athletics and their general manager Billy Beane used a statistical approach that saw them sign players whose skills might be being undervalued on traditional methods of scouting.

You sign players to fulfil particular roles, for example making lots of tackles or making metres, knowing they lack in other areas, so that you can still compete despite being hampered by a budget.

"We're always going to get stuff wrong because whether it's an overseas player or not, you take risks and you gamble," Rush told Sky Sports .

"Context is, and without divulging personal business, it's a salary-cap sport. You're putting certain numbers on players' heads that you believe they're worth.

"Without people knowing the salary-cap value, it's very difficult. It's where that person sits on our cap [that determines] if we get value.

"It's much more detailed than just picking a certain player and saying, 'is he playing well?'

"Waqa Blake played in an NRL Grand Final. That doesn't make him a great player, but for what we had available in our cap or for what we valued the player at, it was worth a chance to do."

So, you gamble and sign what you think is value for money. But did that mean St Helens built a cost-effective squad of players who did not deliver what was asked of them?

One thing that is for sure is that they did not replace like for like.

"I've said it a number of times but Saints' recruitment has been shocking," Sky Sports' Jon Wilkin said.

"It's been terrible. They've made convenient and short-term recruitment choices. They've not replaced like for like and they need to rethink their recruitment strategy.

"There's a lot of young guys who have gone out into Super League who aren't ready. I'm loving that, it is great for them and for their future.

"But the reason they're out there was because you had an old squad at the start of the year that wasn't durable enough to get through a year, and then you signed shoddy replacements for guys who moved on."

Not only that, St Helens are not the spending force they once were. It is not just the 'Super League giants' with cash to burn. Obviously, Wigan have got richer, but Wakefield now have money, as do York, Leigh and more.

More clubs are offering better and Saints are being outcompeted in the wage stakes.

If quality drops, senior players age and suffer injuries, and more is asked of youngsters, then naturally, outcomes of seasons will change.

Lomax and Percival have managed just 14 games between them in 2026. They do not offer what they once did.

Wellens, Roby and Rush also all left the club in a quick span of time. That is three people who have had eyes on St Helens' successes and failures, consistently since the 1990s.

They lost stalwart and skipper Matty Lees to injury early in the season and have not had him as the enforcer on the pitch. They also lost their other enforcer in Morgan Knowles to the NRL.

St Helens fans did not enjoy the attritional approach to rugby under Wellens that brought them third, sixth and fifth-placed finishes that saw them make the play-off semi-finals twice in those three seasons.

The club decided that those results, with the roster available, were not good enough and change was needed. With that, they brought in Paul Rowley to turn the club's fortunes around on a three-year deal.

Rowley lasted less than a season at Saints before being sacked ahead of the fixture against rivals Wigan Warriors in Round 20 back in July.

It is unknown how the season in full would have shaped under Rowley given the raft of injuries that St Helens faced and the clear signs that his systems were not embedding into a club that has a very specific DNA.

What we do know is they finished seventh.

Now they have turned to Australia head coach Kevin Walters to get things back on track.

St Helens legend James Graham said on his podcast, The Bye Round , that he had sent Walters a YouTube video of all of Saints' greatest wins to show him just why they have the tagline 'Never write off the Saints'.

Walters is renowned for maintaining strong environments and being an advocate for his players. He is already teasing big signings he is making.

The noises from St Helens are that they are now reverting to splashing the cash to ensure the quality on the field matches the expectations off it.

The question posed was what was St Helens' 'flap of a wing'. What were the small, incremental changes made that ended in this tornado.

Frankly, it seems that what caused their tornado in 2026 is that they spent four years not flapping their wings at all.

They say in sport, if you are not evolving you are falling behind. Those at St Helens can say they could not see this outcome occurring.

But this is not a random outcome. It was predetermined when option B was chosen - the option of standing still and attempting to not cause disruption by flapping your wings.

The regular Super League season concludes with Round 27 from Thursday September 10 live on Sky Sports.

articles.title: 'Shenzhen win has given us confidence': Satwik-Chirag banish World C'ships heartbreaks, turn focus to Asian Games
articles.summary: Badminton News: NEW DELHI: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty have built a reputation for doing things the hard way. They fall behind, regroup, and more often .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty have built a reputation for doing things the hard way. They fall behind, regroup, and more often than not, find a way back.On Sunday in Shenzhen, that familiar script delivered one of their most important victories of the season. The Indian pair rallied from a set down to defeat China's He Ji Ting and Ren Xiang Yu 11-21, 21-13, 21-17 and lift their maiden China Masters Super 750 title, ending a run of two previous final defeats at the tournament.The triumph was significant beyond the trophy. Just two weeks earlier, Satwik and Chirag had walked away from the World Championships in New Delhi devastated after surrendering a winning position in the quarterfinals. Even their participation in China had been uncertain, with Satwik continuing to manage a chronic shoulder injury and Chirag still wearing support for his lower back - something he's been handling for a-year-and-half.Five grueling matches later, they were back on top of the podium.'Shenzhen gives us confidence'The China Masters has been a curious constant in the Indians' career. They had finished runners-up in 2023 and 2025, but the venue has repeatedly produced some of their strongest performances, even when arriving short of preparation or confidence."We weren't thinking about the fact that we have lost two times in the final there. We were thinking that we have played two finals there. It is kind of like the French Open for us -- we feel very comfortable, stadium feels good, atmosphere feels good," Satwik said.The 26-year-old pointed to a string of encouraging campaigns in Shenzhen across difficult phases of their career."Even this year, we were coming back from injury, wanted confidence and Shenzhen has given that. We always go with the same intent. Whenever we get a chance, we grab that. Only concern was whether body is cooperating or not, if it is not, we wanted to take a step back because of Asian Games but pretty much confident throughout the week," Satwik said.That confidence was tested almost immediately in the final. The Chinese pair dominated the opening game with relentless flat exchanges that prevented the Indians from generating attacking opportunities — a tactical pattern that has troubled them before.But unlike the World Championships, where Satwik's shoulder visibly limited his overhead game, the Indian pair gradually wrestled control of the rallies. They accepted the lifts, dictated the mid-court and allowed Satwik's attack to come alive again. The comeback followed.The difference from World ChampionshipsThe transformation, both insisted, was more physical than mental. "I think it was mainly physical. I think we became much better after the World Championships. We got time, we got off and adjusted," Satwik said.The unusual scheduling of the BWF calendar — with a mandatory Super 750 event two weeks after the World Championships and another fortnight before the Asian Games — had left little room for recovery in Delhi."The World Championship was difficult for us because we didn't have much time (on the court). We played one match, then we played quarterfinals right away. So I think after (the) World Championship, our body kind of gets settled down, used to it. Then we kind of got better. Then we weren't sure as well in China Masters, like how much we can cope up with the body throughout the week. So we just took it one match at a time. So I think overall it was pretty much comfortable throughout the week. That's a good sign going ahead," Satwik said.Chirag echoed that assessment, saying the lack of match rhythm had hurt them more than anything at the World Championships."At the World Championships, we didn't really get a lot of court time as such, especially going into a tough match in the quarterfinals against the Chinese. And we were playing a tournament after almost three odd months. And the first match that we played was very scratchy. I think our body didn't cope as well," Chirag said.The contrast was evident in China. Except for the opening round, every match went the distance, forcing the Indians to endure four three-game contests in succession."Whereas when we played five matches here at the China Open, and we almost played three sets, barring the first round, we played four three sets. And yet I think the body feels a lot better than it was at the World Championship. So I think we got another week of practice going towards the China Masters. That really helped us to do well," Chirag said.Perfect timing before Asian GamesThe focus for the duo now shifts to Japan and the Asian Games, which will be held in Aichi-Nagoya from September 19, where the Indians will defend both their men's doubles gold and India's team silver."We have 10 days to go before we head to Japan. And today was an off day. Obviously, we came only early this morning, so we couldn't really sleep as much. So tomorrow we are back on court training for the Asian Games," Chirag said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
