articles.title: Ex-F1 Boss Bernie Ecclestone Detained at Portuguese Airport for Carrying Shotgun
articles.summary: LISBON, Portugal (AP) — Former Formula 1 boss Bernie Ecclestone was detained at a Portuguese airport on Monday — and released hours later — for possession of a firearm.
articles.body:
LISBON, Portugal (AP) — Former Formula 1 boss Bernie Ecclestone was detained at a Portuguese airport on Monday — and released hours later — for possession of a firearm.

Ecclestone, 95, arrived at Tires Airport near Lisbon, where officers from the Portuguese Public Security Police airport division found a shotgun in his possession for which he lacked a permit.

In an interview with the Daily Mail, Ecclestone admitted he brought the weapon from Switzerland for pigeon shooting.

Will a non-QB be 2027's No. 1 pick? New NFL mock draft

"They asked if I had a blue book, which is apparently the documentation you need, and I told them I never travel with documents like that, any documents at all practically," Ecclestone told the British newspaper. "They said they would arrest me, but after what seemed like hours we sorted it out, but it has been wall-to-wall aggravation."

Ecclestone was at the helm of F1 from 1987-2017, and divides his time between his homes in Switzerland and Portugal.

This is not the first time he has run into trouble for carrying a weapon at an airport. In May 2022 he was detained at Viracopos Airport in Brazil after police found a .32-caliber pistol in his possession. On that occasion he had to pay a fine and was able to leave without further issues.

Ecclestone gained a marketing grip on F1 in the late 1970s by selling its TV rights. Four decades later, the British business magnate controlled the series until his decision to step down. He continues to attend races.

articles.title: Egyptian wrestlers keep vanishing abroad amid a sport in crisis
articles.summary: Two wrestlers have become the latest to flee while abroad, drawing a wave of sympathy as well as legal threats.
articles.body:
Cairo, Egypt – Four days after he disappeared from the Egyptian team camp at the 2026 Under-20 World Wrestling Championships in Slovakia last month, 19-year-old wrestler Ziad Hajjaj Abu Gabal posted a message on Facebook.

“I don’t want my mother and father to be upset with me,” he wrote on August 29. “I did this so I could see myself as a man. I won’t go back to Egypt, my beloved country, until I bring it honour.

“Everything I earn in a month is 700 Egyptian pounds [$13.7], and I’m an international [athlete] … After all this pressure, there was no way I could go back.”

On August 27, another Egyptian wrestler, Mohamed al-Shami, 23, had escaped while his team transited through Rome on their way home from the Mediterranean Games in Taranto, Italy.

In his Facebook post on August 29, Al-Shami said he had come to feel like a financial burden on his family and that he wanted to start earning money for them.

“At a certain point I felt my father was exhausted, that life had become too hard for him,” he wrote. “I’m the eldest of my siblings, so someone had to make a sacrifice and take responsibility.”

While the authorities in Egypt may now try to take legal action against the two athletes, their posts drew a wave of sympathy from Egyptians on Facebook, with many saying they understood the pressures that pushed the athletes to escape from a country mired in poverty .

Indeed, Hajjaj and al-Shami are far from the first Egyptian wrestlers to flee while abroad, and the hardships they describe are widely shared across the sport in Egypt.

A 27-year-old wrestler, who won several gold medals for Egypt and asked not to be named, told Al Jazeera that fellow athletes under 20 years old earn 700 Egyptian pounds ($13.7) to 800 ($15.7) Egyptian pounds a month.

Older international players reportedly receive between 5,000 pounds ($98.2) and 12,000 pounds ($235.7) a month, depending on their achievements.

“Wrestlers often go into debt to cover supplements and living costs while waiting for prize money that may or may not arrive,” he said.

Ahmed Baghdouda left for France in 2023 immediately after winning silver at the African Wrestling Championships, reportedly over low pay. Tarek Abdel Salam defected to Bulgaria in 2017 amid alleged medical neglect and later won European gold under Bulgaria’s flag. That year, Ibrahim Ghanem also chose to stay in France, subsequently winning a World Championship title for the country.

In October 2025, Mohamed Ibrahim el-Sayed – popular as Kishu and a six-time African wrestling champion, two-time U23 world champion, and bronze medallist in the 67kg category at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics – announced he had taken “the first step” towards switching his sporting allegiance to represent the United States, posting training photos from a facility with the US flag behind him.

Asked by Al Jazeera through a messaging app why wrestlers keep fleeing Egypt, Kishu blamed the wrestling federation.

“It’s the only body that can provide a suitable environment, but the opposite keeps happening,” he said from the US. “The problem isn’t just about money – it goes much deeper than that. When I retire, what am I supposed to do? God forbid I get injured – what happens to me then?”

“I would take the same decision again and again and I advise Egypt’s international players to focus on their training and acquire their rights because it’s their lives that are being wasted.”

Al Jazeera reached out to the president and the vice president of the Egyptian Wrestling Federation (EWF), as well as the president of the Egyptian National Olympic Committee (ENOC), for their comments, but none of them responded.

However, the EWF’s team psychologist Hossam Mohamed said the disappearance of players abroad is not simply down to poor financial compensation or neglect, insisting the state provides good support to wrestlers – whether through financial bonuses, training camps abroad, or accommodation and meals. He said medal bonuses can reach 5 million Egyptian pounds ($98,135) for an Olympic gold.

“The wrestling federation, compared to major sports federations, has limited resources in light of the absence of broadcasting rights and the commercial and audience revenues enjoyed by football,” he noted.

“[But the] core problem for [athletes] isn’t only what they receive during their playing years, but what awaits them after retirement or injury.”

On Hajjaj and al-Shami, he said they competed in international championships, but “receiving bonuses is tied to achieving results – a player who doesn’t finish in a top position doesn’t receive a tournament bonus”, and neither was able to achieve podium finishes in recent competitions.

Gamal el-Badrawy, a former head of Egypt’s kickboxing federation, called on the Ministry of Youth and Sports to impose tighter oversight of national sporting federations and to review bonuses, allowances and health insurance.

“[Athletes] cannot be entirely absolved of responsibility, but the weak financial and administrative system is the main driver,” he told Al Jazeera.

Meanwhile, Egypt’s Ministry of Youth and Sports has referred Hajjaj and al-Shami to the public prosecutor, accusing them of breaking the rules governing national delegations.

The ENOC separately referred Brigadier General Ibrahim Adel – EWF secretary-general and head of the wrestling delegation at the tournament in Taranto – to its ethics committee for investigation and suspended him from his duties for allowing al-Shami to escape.

Adel refused to comment on the criticisms against the EWF, but told Al Jazeera he believed the moves against him were unfair, pointing to precautionary measures already in place before the trip: notarised undertakings signed by both the players’ guardians and the players themselves committing them to return to Egypt.

Meanwhile, fleeing athletes often leave behind distressed families.

Hajjaj’s father, Hajjaj Abu Gabal, told Al Jazeera over the phone that he was deeply worried for his son after he left the national team in Slovakia, noting that he had switched off his phone for a long time and did not respond to calls.

“I signed the notarised parental consent required for my underage son to travel,” he said, as 21 is the age of full legal adulthood in Egypt. “But no one from the wrestling federation had contacted me since the escape.”

Hajjaj, according to his father, said wrestling required expenses for food, drink, clothing and other needs, including costs related to the training period and participation in championships, and these expenses were a burden on him and the family.

“Whatever happens, he’s still my son,” the father said.

“I keep praying for him to be safe and secure, and may God compensate him for the difficult times he went through.”

articles.title: Fantasy Football Waiver Wire: Pickups to make before the 2026 season kicks off
articles.summary: We are back with Justin Boone's fantasy football waiver wire series!
articles.body:
Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups. Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

1. Jonah Coleman, RB, Broncos 2. Tyler Allgeier, RB, Cardinals 3. Terrance Ferguson, TE, Rams 4. Ja'Kobi Lane, WR, Ravens 5. Keenan Allen, WR, Colts 6. Kaelon Black, RB, 49ers 7. Tank Bigsby, RB, Eagles 8. Emmett Johnson, RB, Chiefs 9. Malik Willis, QB, Dolphins 10. Dalton Schultz, TE, Texans

With so many great fantasy quarterback options available, Willis often goes undrafted. While you probably don't need to start him in Week 1, you might want to consider stashing the Dolphins dual-threat QB. Willis finished as a top-seven fantasy QB twice in his three relief appearances for the Packers over the last two seasons thanks to rushing totals of 41, 60 and 73 yards. There's also hope Miami's receiving corps is better than initially anticipated with third-round rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas providing a spark.

If you stash Willis and he emerges as a quality fantasy option, you could then contemplate trading your original starting QB for an upgrade at another position.

J.K. Dobbins is healthy entering the season and we all hope this is the year he finally plays all 17 games. However, history has taught us otherwise as the veteran has missed time due to injuries in all six of his NFL campaigns. Though RJ Harvey is the No. 2 back on Denver's depth chart, it's Coleman who projects to benefit the most if Dobbins goes to the blue medical tent again. Sean Payton has raved about the rookie, even comparing his skill set to Dobbins'. In the event of another injury, Coleman is the most likely to step into the lead-back role, while Harvey maintains his change-of-pace, pass-catching back usage.

Don't wait until Dobbins gets hurt, scoop Coleman up now.

Jeremiyah Love is dealing with a high ankle sprain that could limit him early in the season and might even cause him to sit out Week 1. Allgeier is an overqualified backup who showed he can be an NFL starter while posting 1,174 scrimmage yards as a rookie. Even playing behind Bijan Robinson, Allgeier found a way to score eight touchdowns last season. He could occupy a similar role in Arizona, as a weekly TD-or-bust RB3/flex option. If Love can't suit up in the opener, Allgeier will be a fringe low-end fantasy RB2.

Mike Washington Jr. is 56% rostered but would be the No. 2 RB add behind Tyler Allgeier, if available.

Zach Charbonnet is 51% rostered but can be added as an IR stash, if available.

Best one-injury away backup RBs to stash

Lane is coming off an outstanding summer where he impressed everyone in and around the Ravens organization. Whether he can translate that into regular season value remains to be seen, but I want him on my bench while we find out. If Lane is as good as advertised, he could eventually challenge Rashod Bateman for the No. 2 receiver role in a Baltimore offense that's expected to throw more under new coordinator Declan Doyle. Lamar Jackson can certainly use more weapons other than Zay Flowers and a fading Mark Andrews, which is why Lane is occupying a spot on my benches in several leagues.

If you're looking for a more immediate option to slide into your lineup early in the season, Allen is a strong choice. Though Alec Pierce has returned to practice, he's still working his way back from ankle surgery and might start slow in the opening month. The 34-year-old Allen is well past his football prime, but he was the WR13 in fantasy points per game through the first seven weeks last season while playing for the Chargers.

Another hot start could be in the cards for Allen. Just keep in mind, he's also facing a potential suspension at some point due to his recent arrest for a DWI.

Rashid Shaheed is 51% rostered but would be the No. 1 WR add if available.

Jordyn Tyson is 57% rostered but can be added as an IR stash, if available.

Ferguson was the 46th overall pick in last year's draft and despite being buried on the depth chart for most of his rookie campaign, he managed to make a fantasy impact on several occasions. In the five games where he saw at least three targets, Ferguson posted 50 yards and/or a touchdown four times. Ferguson also finished the season with double-digit fantasy points in back to back contests, while Tyler Higbee was sidelined. Even with the crowded nature of the Rams' TE room, Ferguson's speed and pass-catching chops allow him to line up in the slot or out wide, making him a mismatch nightmare for defenses.

With Puka Nacua expected to play through a hip/groin injury in Week 1 and Davante Adams turning 34 in December, it's not out of the question that Ferguson becomes a key part of the passing game during his sophomore season. I'll be stashing him on my bench through the Rams' season opener on Thursday, just to see if he gets enough usage to be fantasy relevant.

Schultz is a more boring fantasy option, but also offers low-end TE1 potential following the season-ending injury to wideout Jayden Higgins. The veteran tight end is quietly coming off a strong fantasy campaign where he averaged the 11th-most points at his position over the final 13 weeks. That included finishing tied for third in receptions among tight ends (82) and sixth in receiving yards (777). Aside from Nico Collins, the Texans don't have any established pass-catchers in the offense, so Schultz has a chance to be C.J. Stroud's No. 2 target once again.

You're not going to impress your leaguemates by taking the 30-year-old Texans tight end, but Schultz is in the group of high-end TE2s who could easily end the year as a top-12 starter at the position.

articles.title: College volleyball players keep Wrigley Field crowd entertained during delays
articles.summary: More than 40,000 college volleyball fans left Chicago’s Wrigley Field Sunday night without getting to watch the Nebraska-Missouri match due to weather delays, but it was still a win with players doing their best to keep the crowd entertained — with a dance competition.
articles.body: More than 40,000 college volleyball fans left Chicago’s Wrigley Field Sunday night without getting to watch the Nebraska-Missouri match due to weather delays, but it was still a win with players doing their best to keep the crowd entertained — with a dance competition. The NCAA hosted two women’s volleyball matches at the iconic baseball field on Sunday night. The first one, between the University of Kentucky and Penn State University, went off with no problems. But once night fell for the University of Nebraska and University of Missouri game, the outdoor court became hazardous due to the humid conditions. Players for both teams were seen slipping and sliding while trying to make their plays. The match was delayed as crews tried to dry the court off and players even joined in with towels at one point to help speed the process up. According to the NCAA website, the logo at the center of the court was also ripped off to help improve court traction. Players from both teams wanted to keep the energy up in the face of the delays. In the spirit of competition, the two teams started a dance battle while everyone waited. There were 43,067 people in the stands Sunday night. It’s the second-most attended women’s volleyball event in the league’s history, according to the NCAA. More than 92,000 people attended the 2023 match at Memorial Stadium in Nebraska. Despite best efforts to get the match back on track, the court still wasn’t dry enough, and a decision was made to suspend the match due to the court surface issues. The University of Nebraska said in a statement that it was not possible to reschedule at Wrigley Field. A post to the team’s Facebook page thanked the Cornhuskers fans for an unforgettable night in spite of it all. “There are truly no greater fans in college volleyball and we thank you for always coming along for the ride!” the post said. “None of this would be possible without you!” It was an emotional moment for the players. Multiple seniors from Nebraska’s team apologized to their fans, who were the majority in the stands, after the decision was announced. “We wanted to give you guys our all and we didn’t do that tonight,” said Bergen Reilly, a setter for Nebraska. After the emotional speeches, Nebraska’s Andi Jackson took over the microphone and started to sing Kelly Clarkson’s “Since You Been Gone.” She then ran over to the Missouri players to have them join in. Jackson waved over the teammates as both schools players huddled around the mic to sing some of the song a cappella for the crowd before they went home.

articles.title: Qinwen Zheng stuns Iga Swiatek with another remarkable US Open comeback
articles.summary: Zheng, who arrived at the US Open as a qualifier due to an injury-hit 2025 season, won a second match in a row having trailed 0-5 in a set
articles.body:
Qinwen Zheng continued her extraordinary US Open run as she produced a comeback from 0-5 down in a set for the second match in a row to knock out six-time grand slam champion Iga Swiatek and reach the quarter-finals.

Former Olympic champion Zheng, who defeated Swiatek in the gold medal match in Paris two years ago, had to qualify to reach the main draw of the US Open. The Chinese star missed long stretches of the 2025 season due to an elbow injury and had fallen to No 121 in the rankings.

After qualifying for the main draw and reaching the third round, Zheng trailed former Australian Open champion Madison Keys 0-5 and was match point down in the third set before winning seven consecutive games to win 1-6 7-6 (7-3) 7-5 against the American 22nd seed.

Two days later against the eighth seed and former US Open champion Swiatek, Zheng trailed 0-5 in the first yet produced the same trick, winning seven games in a row to clinch the set. She then converted the only break of serve in the second set to win 7-5 6-3 and reach the quarter-finals of the US Open for the third time.

Zheng fell onto her back after converting her fourth match point. She has now won seven matches in a row in New York. "Well, honestly, I have to say, I started the match not so well," she said. "Little by little I found my rhythm on the center court because it's been a long, long time. I just really appreciate it to be here in the Ashe Stadium.

"I just focused point by point and little by little I start to play better tennis, I start to find my game and in one moment I even forgot the score in the first set at 4-5. That shows how I'm focused. I guess to come back 0-5 yesterday is not lucky, that's all I can say.

"I'm just really happy to win this match cause it's not easy and it's been a while really. I didn't beat any top 10 player. I just really, really appreciated this win for me, and I want to say thank you for all the fans who come to support me today."

For Swiatek, defeat to Zheng brought a familiar story and the former Wimbledon champion left Arthur Ashe Stadium in tears. The Pole's error count spiralled, finishing with 28 in total. Swiatek's last five exits from the grand slams since winning Wimbledon in 2025 have also come in straight-sets.

Zheng will play either second seed Elena Rybakina or 13th seed Naomi Osaka, the two-time US Open champion, in the quarter-finals. Earlier, French Open champion Mirra Andreeva produced her own comeback to defeat Anastasia Potapova 5-7 6-4 6-3 and reach her first US Open quarter-final.

Potopova was also in floods of tears as her stay in New York came to an end. The 25-year-old, who represents Austria, won the first set against fifth seed Andreeva, but, at 5-3 down in the third she badly twisted her knee chasing a forehand down.

Potopova had the knee heavily strapped up and bravely finished the match, but did not win another point. "Anastasia is a good friend, and seeing what a battle we have and then seeing her fall is not easy," said Russian teenager Andreeva. "It's not the way you want to finish the match. I just told her she is playing amazing and I'm sure she'll come back even stronger, she's a warrior."

articles.title: Oregon stock report: Jeremiah McClellan surges in win vs. Boise State
articles.summary: Who helped or hurt their stock for Oregon in Week 1? Breaking down the biggest risers and fallers after the Ducks’ game against Boise State.
articles.body:
After months of trying to forecast what we might see from this Oregon Ducks team in 2026 and who the standout players would be, Saturday's 34-27 win over the Boise State Broncos gave us real data to take in and use to form opinions.

We're no longer taking sound bites and tips from sources about which players may be stepping up; now we have real on-field play to evaluate.

In Oregon's season-opening win, we got a lot of great information on players who are going to have bigger-than-anticipated impacts, and others who may not end up playing as big of a role as we might have expected. With 497 yards of total offense, there were several players on that side of the ball who showed out, while the defense had a nice day as well, stepping up in big moments.

So let's evaluate what we saw and take away who we are encouraged by and who needs to show us more going forward. Here is our weekly stock report after the first game of the season.

Stat Line: 6 catches, 150 yards, 1 TD — 76.1 PFF Grade

Analysis: There were a lot of people in Eugene who knew about Oregon Ducks WR Jeremiah McClellan ahead of the Week 1 game vs. Boise State, but he's starting to become well-known around the college football world at large after that game. McClellan stood out in a deep group of wide receivers and looked like the clear No. 1 pass-catcher on an offense full of talent. Of course, this will likely change week by week with as many mouths as there are to feed in Eugene, but McClellan was undoubtedly the biggest winner of the week for the Ducks.

Stat Line: 2 tackles, 0.5 TFL, 2 QB Hits — 73.5 PFF Grade

Analysis: The biggest riser on the defense in my mind was linebacker Dylan Williams, who played a huge role in this game, stepping up alongside Jerry Mixon and Devon Jackson in that linebacker room. While his stats don't jump off the page, Williams was flying around the field and had a huge impact on this game, earning some high praise from Dan Lanning when all was said and done. Expect to see a lot more of Williams this year.

Analysis: In his first game as a Duck, nickel cornerback Carl Williams IV struggled a bit. While he was able to get in on a few tackles, he wasn't great in coverage, giving up Boise State's first touchdown of the day after getting beat on the outside, and he ultimately earned a 54.7 coverage grade on Pro Football Focus. It's early in the year, and there will undoubtedly be some growth here, but Williams needs to show more going forward.

Stat Line: 1 tackle, 1 Pass Break-Up — 66.0 PFF Grade

Analysis: Na'eem Offord played far better than the stats show on Saturday, and he had a huge impact, particularly late in the game, with some great coverage and a massive pass break-up on Boise State's final play of the game. Offord is in a tight competition/rotation with Ify Obidegwu, so performances like this are very encouraging to see.

Stat Line: 0 sacks allowed, 2 QB pressures allowed — 64.4 PFF Grade

Analysis: A lot of people were surprised on Saturday when it was Ziyare Addison who came onto the field as the starting left tackle instead of Fox Crader, but Addison lived up to the expectations, protecting the blindside and looking very good doing it. Adison was one of three offensive linemen to play every snap of the game, and it appears that he is going to be the guy for the Ducks going forward at that spot.

Stat Line: No Offensive Snaps — 4 Special Teams Snaps

Analysis: Going into this game, I expected to see Kawika Rogers as one of the first offensive linemen off the bench, and potentially even in the starting lineup. Instead, we didn't see him at all on the field, with Trent Ferguson coming in as relief at the left guard spot instead. We will see if that changes going forward, but I'll definitely be watching it over the next couple of weeks.

Stat Line: 2-for-2 FGs (26-, 44-yards), 4-for-4 PATs

Analysis: It was quiet and flew under the radar, but something needs to be said for Gage Hurych's performance on Saturday. As a kicker, the best thing you can do is go unnoticed, do your job when asked, and make field goals when given the opportunity. That's what Hurych did, which is encouraging for Oregon fans after an offseason of relative uncertainty at this position.

Analysis: As a wide receiver, Evan Stewart was great on Saturday, with eight catches for 72 yards. As a punt returner, though, Stewart left a bit to be desired. He had a trio of mistakes: a fair catch at the 3-yard line and two muffed punts, one of which was recovered by Boise State. In the end, Oregon was still able to get the win, and Lanning expressed support of Stewart after the game, but it's clear that this operation needs to clean up going forward for the Ducks, or we may see someone else back there in the return game.

Stat Line: 8 tackles, 1 sack — 73.5 PFF Grade

Analysis: As a whole, the Oregon defensive line played pretty well on Saturday, but Bear Alexander absolutely stood out among the biggest difference-makers. He was very solid in the run game and was able to rack up four QB pressures and one sack. Going into the year, Alexander was often listed as the fourth DL in a great quartet, but he was anything but 4th best on Saturday.

Contact/Follow @Ducks_Wire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Oregon Ducks news, notes, and opinion s.

articles.body:
Daniel Maldini's first goal in a Cagliari shirt was also worth three hugely important points for the Sardinians.

Daniel Maldini's goal was the only and decisive one of the match, even though both teams had several chances to make the game much more high-scoring, especially the home side. There was no shortage of controversy late on over a Gagliardini-Ndri collision in the box, which Sacchi and VAR waved away, but which according to DAZN 's replay analysis was a penalty.

Di Francesco thus suffers another defeat, while Cagliari celebrate three vital points but must also deal with the negative news of Mattia Felici's injury, which forced him to leave the pitch just 13 minutes after coming on.

🚑 Felici, what bad luck: injured after just 13 minutes

In the second half, in the 61st minute, Mattia Felici came on for Fazzini and made an immediate impact, troubling Lecce with his bursts of pace. After just 13 minutes, however, during a sprint with Gallo, he suddenly pulled up with a problem in his left leg. The player was forced to leave the field visibly distraught.

⚽ Maldini, first three-point goal for Cagliari!

Daniel Maldini's first goal in a Cagliari shirt was worth three hugely important points. Fazzini delivered a perfect corner and found Maldini, who got ahead of the defense and beat Falcone with a precise header.

⚠️ Gagliardini-Ndri, Marelli has no doubts about the penalty

Late on, with both teams exhausted and spaces now wide open, Gagliardini took a big risk with a collision in the box with Ndri, who went to ground. Referee Sacchi allowed play to continue and VAR decided not to call him over to the monitor.

According to Luca Marelli, DAZN's refereeing analyst, there were indeed grounds for a penalty: in his view, Gagliardini did not get the ball in his challenge on Ndri. A bit of chaos then broke out during the final onslaught, but the outcome did not change: Cagliari took home the win.

articles.title: Bill Belichick insists he's in control at UNC. The investigation could test that claim
articles.summary: Bill Belichick defended North Carolina football's culture amid an ongoing investigation, but key questions about the program remain unanswered.
articles.body:
Four days after North Carolina football general manager Michael Lombardi resigned amid a university investigation into his conduct and the football program, Tar Heels coach Bill Belichick addressed the media for the first time since UNC's Week 0 win over TCU in Dublin .

"Understand the importance of the work that's being done by the investigative team and, obviously, our high standard here, our code of conduct, doing things the right way and making sure that our student-athletes are given the utmost, best treatment, the very best care and very best coaching that we can possibly give them," Belichick said during his opening statement on Monday, Sept. 7.

Lombardi was placed on paid administrative leave on July 27. Though the school declined to elaborate on the move, multiple reports stated a former North Carolina employee had filed a human resources complaint against Lombardi.

Bill Belichick, UNC football open Year 2 with win over TCU in Ireland

Ahead of every news conference this season, a university spokesperson has said players and members of the coaching staff are prohibited from discussing the investigation.

On Monday, the first football question of Belichick's 18-minute news conference didn't come until the 13-minute mark. Most questions centered around the culture within the program under Belichick and the university's ongoing investigation. Belichick's son, Steve, remains on medical leave from his role as the team's defensive coordinator. No further details have been provided on his situation since Bill Belichick announced on Aug. 6 his son was away from the program.

"I love all my kids, but I'm not going to comment on a medical situation," Belichick said when asked about his son's situation. Belichick also said there were "no updates" on the status of the general manager and defensive coordinator roles.

"It's kind of the way it's been here for the last few weeks," he said. "We've kind of redistributed some things. We'll stay with that for the time being."

Dean Stoyer, the university's vice chancellor for communications, and athletic director Steve Newmark were present for Belichick's news conference. The 74-year-old coach didn't address specifics about the questions being asked by investigators, but said "we'll see what the answers are. I don't know."

In its news release regarding Lombardi's departure, the university said it "continues its ongoing investigation and will consider all appropriate corrective actions responsive to the information it learns." WRAL reported investigators were asking troubling questions about the culture within the program.

"In the end, we want to run a program in the very best way," Belichick said. "If there's things we need to do to correct it, we'll obviously do 'em."

Bill Belichick contract: What would UNC owe if it fired coach?

Belichick's contract states he is required to adhere to UNC's policies, along with the "regulations and rules that apply to this position." It also requires him to "promote an atmosphere of compliance" and report any potential violations.

When asked if he believes the program has an atmosphere of compliance, Belichick said "yeah, totally." He also said he's "aware of all the NCAA rules." Asked if there are indicators that he's in control of the program, Belichick said "if you're around here every day, I think you'd see it."

If UNC decided to fire Belichick for cause, the university wouldn't have to pay out anything. If the school were to fire him without cause, it would owe Belichick what he was set to earn through Dec. 31, 2027 . The first three years of his five-year contract are guaranteed, meaning he stands to earn $30 million across the guaranteed period of his contract.

Belichick earns $10.1 million in annual compensation . His contract, though, includes $0 in financial severance if he's fired in the final two seasons of his term.

"My main focus is to coach the football team. That's where I put my time and energy," Belichick said. ". … Obviously, everybody's responsible — including me — for doing things properly. And we intend to do that."

Is UNC football investigation affecting players?

Belichick was also asked about how he's approaching conversations about the investigation with his players, saying honesty is the focus of his communication with the team.

"I keep them informed and do the best I can — and our staff does the best they can — to do a good job of staying on top of players, holding them accountable for the things that they need to do on and off the field as student-athletes and as football players," he said.

Like Belichick, captains Christo Kelly and Benjamin Hall are putting their energy into football and preparing for the home opener, Sept. 12 against East Tennessee State .

"We don't really focus on anything like that," Kelly said when asked about the questions surrounding the program.

"We're here to play football. The bond in the locker room is so strong. That's not really anything that we're kind of focused on, worried about in any sense of the imagination."

Hall echoed those thoughts about the off-the-field questions and possible distractions for the Tar Heels with an ongoing investigation.

"I'm gonna be honest with you. No one or anyone in this building is losing any sleep over that," Hall said.

"… We're so focused everything internal and getting better on the field, getting better in the meeting room, we couldn't care less about what we see in the headlines or what's on the news. It's not gonna affect this team."

Rodd Baxley covers North Carolina Tar Heels athletics for The Fayetteville Observer as part of the USA TODAY Network. Follow his ACC coverage on X/Twitter or Bluesky: @RoddBaxley. Got questions regarding UNC? Send them to rbaxley@usatodayco.com.

articles.title: Koopmeiners always knew he would remain at Juventus this season
articles.summary: Teun Koopmeiners was linked with a summer move away from Juventus after two disappointing seasons at the club, and Juve were keen for him to leave.The Dutchm...
articles.body:
Teun Koopmeiners was linked with a summer move away from Juventus after two disappointing seasons at the club, and Juve were keen for him to leave .

The Dutchman has failed to replicate the form he showed at Atalanta, which prompted Juventus to add him to their squad, and the Bianconeri wanted him to leave.

They waited for offers, but those offers started arriving late in the window , and it was never a good time for Juve to sell him or any other midfielder in their squad.

Koopmeiners has not regained a starting spot in the team, and he might not do so, but the Dutchman is not thinking about leaving as much as the club wants him to go.

While the rumours were flying around during the summer, he remained relaxed because he wanted to stay and did not consider leaving the Bianconeri for any reason.

Koopmeiners wanted to remain at Juventus

Now that the transfer window is shut, Koopmeiners can focus on doing well this season, but he never thought about leaving Juventus.

The Dutchman appears determined to contribute to the team despite his difficult spell at the club. His priority remains helping the Bianconeri rather than considering a move away.

Koopmeiners has therefore continued to focus on his role within the squad, even though he has not yet regained a regular starting position.

(Photo by Pier Marco Tacca/Getty Images)

Speaking via Tuttomercatoweb , Koopmeiners explained that he never had any doubt about remaining at Juventus. He said:

"I don't know… For me there was no doubt that I would stay, I always remained focused on how I could help the team. I started well, but I'm thinking about the team."

His comments make it clear that leaving Juve was never his priority during the summer. While his future was the subject of speculation, Koopmeiners remained focused on helping the Bianconeri.

The midfielder now has the opportunity to concentrate fully on the season ahead and attempt to improve his situation at Juventus. Despite the uncertainty surrounding his future during the transfer window, he remained committed to staying at the club.

Those two players were rookie tight end Will Kacmarek and linebacker/safety Ronnie Harrison Jr. However, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley told the media on Monday that both are expected to practice this afternoon.

articles.title: The Rams’ middle linebackers could be the key to an all-time great defense
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES - - — The Los Angeles Rams have assembled a defense with the potential to become something special.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES - - — The Los Angeles Rams have assembled a defense with the potential to become something special.

With Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald leading a defensive front that also features Byron Young, Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske and Poona Ford, while Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson headline a revamped secondary, the Rams have legitimate playmakers at nearly every level.

But if this defense is going to become more than simply one of the NFL's best and wants to be viewed and remembered as one of the greatest defenses in franchise history, the middle linebacker position could be the difference.

That responsibility falls heavily on two men: Nate Landman and Omar Speights.

Landman and Speights aren't likely to receive the same attention as Garrett or Donald or the other names on this defense and that's understandable. The pass rush will create the highlights, while the secondary will get the interceptions and pass breakups.

But somebody has to clean up everything that happens in between.

That's where the Rams' inside linebackers become so important.

Landman enters 2026 coming off a career year. He started all 17 games in 2025, finishing with 132 tackles, eight tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks, five quarterback hits, an interception, five passes defended, four forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries. He also served as the team's on-field signal caller, wearing the green dot.

Speights was just as important to the defense's development, starting all 16 games he played in while finishing with 85 tackles.

Now, the Rams need both players to take another step.

The defensive line can create chaos, but even the best fronts won't win every snap. Offensive linemen will occasionally reach the second level. Running backs will find creases. Quarterbacks will escape pressure.

When those plays happen, Landman and Speights have to be there.

They have to diagnose quickly and make plays on the ball.

Perhaps what's most important is that they have to cover.

That's especially important in today's NFL, where offenses constantly use running backs and tight ends to attack linebackers in space.

The Rams can have Garrett, Donald and co. collapsing the pocket, but if the linebackers can't hold up behind them, opposing quarterbacks will find ways to exploit the defense.

Chris Shula has already seen the value of Landman's presence.

Last season, the Rams' defensive coordinator credited the team's improved run defense to better execution and personnel changes, specifically mentioning Landman.

The Rams will need that same discipline in 2026.

Inside linebackers coach Greg Williams has also emphasized the importance of adapting to the way opponents attack the defense, while praising Landman's impact and the continued development of the position group.

That's where Landman's leadership becomes especially valuable.

He's not simply responsible for making tackles.

He's responsible for getting everyone lined up, communicating the calls and making sure the defense is operating as one unit.

That responsibility becomes even more important when you consider the number of new pieces around him.

"I've always grown up in the defense where the middle linebacker is kind of the quarterback of the defense directing traffic," Landman said previously. "That's the place where I feel comfortable in."

The Rams don't need Landman and Speights to make every play.

If Garrett beats his blocker but the quarterback escapes, somebody has to clean it up.

If Donald occupies multiple blockers and a running back finds a crease, somebody has to fill it.

If the secondary forces a quarterback to check the ball down, somebody has to prevent a five-yard completion from becoming a 30-yard gain.

Head coach Sean McVay has consistently emphasized the importance of clarity and communication within his football teams. With a defense containing this much talent, the Rams need players in the middle who can make sure everyone is on the same page and allow the front seven to play fast.

That's part of what makes Landman so valuable.

As for Speights, 2026 represents another opportunity to prove that his development can take this defense to another level.

Speights already has significant starting experience, and the Rams' current depth chart lists him and Landman as the starting inside linebackers.

The chemistry between the two could become one of the most important elements of the defense.

McVay is very confident in what this group can accomplish heading into the season.

"I feel really good about that inside linebacker group. 'G-Money' [Inside Linebackers Coach Greg Williams] does a great job coaching those guys up. Landman is outstanding. I think he's had a really good camp. He's got great ownership, communication abilities," McVay said. "And same thing, Omar does an amazing job with that as well. His knockback tackles, his ability to be able to be productive in both phases. Both those guys are studs.

With Los Angles heavily invested in creating pressure and forcing quarterbacks into uncomfortable situations. The secondary has the talent to capitalize when quarterbacks are forced to hold the ball.

Landman and Speights are the bridge between those two groups.

McVay also likes with the rest of the group can offer the team as well.

"I think Shaun Dolac has had an outstanding camp. He can play either inside backer spot. [He's] got good range, good understanding. And then adding Grant Stuard to the mix has been really powerful. He's obviously a special team stud, but he's also been really productive when he's played that. So I feel really good about those four guys."

If this group can consistently stop the run, cover in space and clean up mistakes when things break down up front, the Rams' defense could have the complete formula necessary to become historically good.

But don't overlook the players in the middle.

Because if Landman, Speights and others can become the glue that holds everything together, the Rams could have something far more dangerous than a talented defense.

articles.title: Demond Williams' Legs Play Hero for Washington in Apple Cup
articles.summary: In several key moments, Demond Williams Jr.'s legs helped power the Washington Huskies to a win in the Apple Cup.
articles.body:
Entering the season, Washington's running game had a major question mark around it. Who would the lead back be? Who was going to be Jedd Fisch's go-to guy in crunch-time? Well, that question was answered for a brief moment Sunday afternoon.

That answer was quarterback Demond Williams Jr., who led the Huskies ' rushing attack with 7 carries for 61 yards and a touchdown.

After starting running back Quaid Carr left the game with an injury, Oregon transfer Jayden Limar stepped into the backfield. However, with the Huskies' offense struggling to put up points, the dual-threat signal caller took things upon himself. In the second quarter, following an interception from first-year cornerback Jeron Jones, Williams evaded the pocket for a 16-yard rush on third-and-10.

Two plays later, Williams scampered his way into the front corner of the end zone to help Washington jump out to a 10-0 lead.

Late in the fourth, the veteran quarterback found himself in a very similar predicament. After a false start, the Huskies were facing third-and-9 with just over three minutes to play. Once again, Williams rolled out left, evaded three Cougar defenders, and turned upfield for a 21-yard gain. The drive would result in a Limar touchdown, putting the game out of reach at 24-10.

"That scramble to convert (the third down) was what we know Demond can do, and is, and his feet are one of our biggest advantages," Fisch said after the game. "There's no question about it, and his ability to make that first guy miss and break that tackle made a huge difference."

The pair of pivotal third-down plays made up for half of Washington's third-down conversions, and ultimately led to 14 of the Huskies' 24 points.

From a promising freshman to now the cornerstone of the offense, the junior and his team have lofty aspirations for what they can accomplish this year. Although Sunday's showing certainly won't be enough for the Huskies to reach those goals, it did prove that their leader can make big plays when the Huskies need him most.

MARSHALL, Texas ( KTAL/KMSS ) — The Marshall Independent School District (MISD) has announced details for upcoming celebrations to honor two legendary football coaches.

MISD will name the athletic pavilion in honor of Coach Bill Harper and the football field in honor of Coach Dennis Parker.

On September 11, 2026, at the Marshall High School (MHS) Cafeteria at 5:30 p.m., Coach Harper will be honored with a reception at the MHS Cafeteria. The reception will be followed by an on-field presentation at 6:30 p.m., and kickoff at 7 p.m.

There will be a meet-and-greet with Coach Parker on September 17 at the MHS Library at 7:30 p.m. On September 18, there will be a reception in the MHS cafeteria at 6:00 p.m., followed by an on-field presentation at 7:00 p.m., and kickoff at 7:30 p.m.

Coach Harper served as an assistant coach and the defensive coordinator at MHS for the 1990 5A Division I (commonly known as Big 5A) State Championship campaign

He took over as head coach in 1991 after Coach Parker departed to coach the University of North Texas (UNT) and filled the role until 2001.

Coach Harper retired from coaching in 2002, but returned to the sidelines in 2005 when he became the head coach and athletic director in Nacogdoches. In 2007, he ended a 15-year playoff drought for the Dragons.

Coach Parker took the head coaching job at MHS in 1984, years removed from the Mavericks' last playoff win in 1949.

In just four years, Coach Parker and the Mavericks won the district championship before falling to Dallas Carter in the quarterfinals.

Carter would later have their state championship, and entire season, overturned due to a grade-changing scandal, making Marshall the first Texas team to have an undefeated season in the record books but not win a state championship. For that feat, Parker was named Texas High School Coach of the Year, an award almost exclusively won by state championship coaches.

In 1990, just six years after Coach Parker arrived, he and the Mavericks won their Big 5A state championship. He left after the season to coach the University of North Texas.

MISD previously named the track after Coach Emma Bennett, who led the Lady Mavs to 10 consecutive district championships in the 80s and 90s, and the fieldhouse after Marshall native NFL Hall of Famer Y.A. Tittle.

On Wednesday night, the Seattle Seahawks will start their title defense campaign against the New England Patriots. Originally, he was a defensive coach, until 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan moved him to the offensive side of the ball during the 2020 season. Eventually, he became the tight ends coach in 2022 and even added the responsibilities of being the run game coordinator last year. The Seahawks have turned the tide back to their favor in this rivalry, having won the last two games in dominant fashion. articles.summary: CBS shared an injury update on Iowa running back LJ Phillips Jr. on Monday.
articles.body:
The Iowa football program got a big injury update on running back LJ Phillips Jr. on Monday.

According to a report from Matt Zenitz and Chris Hummer of CBS Sports, it is believed that Phillips suffered a high ankle sprain in the Hawkeyes ' 40-0 win over Northern Illinois on Saturday. Phillips limped off the field near the end of the first quarter and didn't return to the game.

High ankle sprain recovery times can be tricky to evaluate. Depending on the severity of the sprain, a player can miss anywhere from 2-12 weeks. A recovery timeline for a typical high ankle sprain usually falls in the 4-6 week range. If that's the case for Phillips, he could be out until Iowa 's bye week, which falls in just over six weeks. That would mean he misses all three games against Michigan , Ohio State , and Washington .

Before the injury, Phillips had four carries for five yards in the game. Last season at South Dakota, he rushed for 1,921 yards and 19 touchdowns. There should be more updates on his timeline when Kirk Ferentz speaks to the media on Tuesday.

articles.title: Notre Dame Football Stats: Week 1 Review of Win over Wisconsin
articles.summary: Let’s take a look at the numbers from Notre Dame’s 41-13 win over Wisconsin.
articles.body:
Another Notre Dame college football season opener is in the books and there are two constants for me:

Dealing with the traditional, emotional first game roller coaster despite how much I convinced myself this time would be different

Stumbling through how to tell an analytics story without any real points of reference

Fortunately, the Irish delivered a big win that made all of the Week 1 stress worth it.

The final score for the game was 41-13 and Notre Dame had a solid handle on things from beginning to end. Most of the not fun moments for ND fans were concentrated in the game's first half.

Notre Dame outscored Wisconsin 10-3 in the first quarter and the Badgers flipped the script with a 7-3 run to close out the second quarter. But the Irish recorded 14 points in each of the remaining quarters while Wisconsin was only able to score three in the third quarter.

The Irish were +66 in total yards earned during their Week 1 matchup, tallying up 350 yards compared with the Badgers' 284 yards. And they had the advantage in both the passing and rushing categories.

Mike Denbrock's offense was +22 in passing yards, edging out Wisconsin 239-217. The details behind both team's passing performances were pretty similar. They both logged 19 pass completions, though Wisconsin made 30 attempts and Notre Dame made 29 attempts. One of the biggest passing blemishes for the game landed on the Wisconsin side, with one interception thrown late in the third quarter.

Notre Dame had a substantial rushing advantage. They beat out Wisconsin with a +44 differential, out earning their opponent 111-67 on the ground. But neither squad was particularly efficient in terms of rushing. The Irish had 32 rush attempts and finished with an average of 3.5 yards per attempt. The Badgers closed out things with 31 carries and averaged 2.2 yards per carry.

C.J. Carr got the 2026-27 season started in a solid way, picking up where he left off from last year's standout freshman performance. Carr threw the ball more in the season opener than he did on average last season but all the other stats held mostly the same. He completed 19 of his attempts for a 66% completion rate. He logged 239 yards and also threw two passing touchdowns.

Notre Dame continued the recent tradition of utilizing a rushing committee, with three running backs carrying the load in Week 1.

Junior running back Aneyas Williams led the group with 20 carries for 90 yards. He averaged 4.5 yards per carry and was responsible for both of the team's collective rushing touchdowns.

Senior Jordan Faison led the receiver room during Week 1 with four catches for 81 yards.

Sophomore running back Nolan James Jr. stood out as the Irish's most prominent dual threat. James Jr. had seven rush attempts for 19 yards but produced significantly more in the receiving category. He closed out the Wisconsin game with four catches for 67 yards and one touchdown through the air.

Junior wide receiver Micah Gilbert logged three receptions for 34 yards and senior tight end Cooper Flanagan pulled down two catches for 13 yards.

Notre Dame's defense got off to a slow start but turned things around.

Senior linebacker Kahanu Kia recovered a fumble on special teams and senior cornerback DJ McKinney was responsible for a 55-yard interception return for a touchdown.

The Irish defensive unit finished Week 1 with two sacks, six tackles for loss and five pass deflections.

Senior defensive lineman Boubacar Traore knabbed three solo tackles, one sack and two tackles for loss.

Junior defensive lineman Francis Brewu closed out the Wisconsin game with three tackles, one sack and one tackle for loss.

Sophomore cornerback Jayden Sanders led the secondary with two pass deflections.

The remaining deflections were spread across cornerbacks DJ McKinney and Leonard more as well as safety Brauntae Johnson.

One of the most reassuring things about how Notre Dame won their season opener was the offensive stability that emerged as the game progressed.

The team's first scoring drive was capped off with a field goal and took four plays spanning 48 yards. They scored a passing touchdown built on a four-play, 13-yard drive to close out the first quarter. But the rest of the Irish's points resulted from long, relatively efficient drives:

It was a solid start to the 2026-27 CFB season for Notre Dame. Would it have been great if my stress levels were just a smidge lower during the first half? A resounding yes.

But we've got a long fall of football ahead of us and this performance has me feeling pretty optimistic about what the Irish can deliver.

Former Celtic goalkeeping target Asmir Begovic has revealed he held talks with the Hoops over a potential move to Parkhead.

The 39-year-old is currently without a club after leaving Leicester City at the end of last season and was heavily linked with Celtic following Joe Hart's retirement in 2024.

Celtic ultimately opted to bring in Kasper Schmeichel as their new No.1, while the subsequent arrival of Sam Johnstone from Wolves has left Martin O'Neill well stocked between the posts.

Begovic has now confirmed there was genuine interest from Celtic in the past, while revealing he also held discussions with Rangers.

Begovic told Hajper: "Celtic definitely interested me. I've had some conversations in the past with both Celtic and Rangers, but unfortunately a move never materialised.

"There are many factors in making deals happen, but you can't ignore how big those two football clubs are in terms of tradition. I actually love the SPFL in general, it's a very competitive league and the intensity is always there.

"It's something that we in England really relate to and respect. It never worked out, and while I think time is running out for that to happen, I have huge respect for both clubs, their tradition, and their history."

Begovic also worked under former Celtic managerial target Eddie Howe during his time at Bournemouth, with the Englishman again being linked with the Parkhead job once O'Neill eventually steps aside.

Howe came close to taking charge of Celtic in 2021 before talks collapsed and Ange Postecoglou was subsequently appointed. He is now available again after leaving Newcastle United in July, having guided the Magpies to EFL Cup glory in 2025.

However, Begovic believes his former manager could have his sights set on one of football's biggest jobs.

He added: "Eddie Howe to Celtic? I think Eddie Howe will be looking at some of the biggest jobs in the world, and that's probably where he sees himself.

"What he did at Newcastle is absolutely incredible, he left at a good time and his stock is at a really high point. He's always been linked with the England job, rightly so, and I could see that happening down the line. Anytime a massive job comes up, he has to be in the running.

Baltimore is set to kick off the 2026 season on the road against the Indianapolis Colts , and one position to watch will be the linebacker spot opposite All-Pro Roquan Smith. articles.title: Rules expert Mike Pereira on Michigan's time controversy: 'Use the TV video'
articles.summary: Michigan football's stunning win over Western Michigan continues to befuddle even the most seasoned rules analysts.
articles.body:
Michigan football 's stunning win over Western Michigan continues to befuddle even the most seasoned rules analysts.

Fox rules expert Mike Pereira said in an interview with The Athletic that the explanation of a more official game clock granting Michigan the extra second it needed to complete a Hail Marry pass and avoid an upset doesn't jive with what he knows of these rulings.

"It is my understanding that if there is a discrepancy between the video and replay command center versus the television network video that everybody sees, that replay is to use the TV video," Pereira said. "And that is the same protocol in the NFL, in the UFL. It's the same. You use the footage that everybody sees if there is a discrepancy."

With 9 seconds left in the game on Saturday, Sept. 5, U-M quarterback Bryce Underwood heaved a Hail Mary from midfield through the back of the end zone, apparently ending the game as a 12-7 WMU victory. The clocks on the TV broadcast – and the video boards at the stadium – showed no time left.

After a video review, however, officials determined the ball was touched by a formerly out-of-bounds WMU defender with 1 second left and restored that on the clock, allowing another play. Underwood than connected with receiver JJ Buchanan on a second Hail Mary for a 13-12 win.

The Big Ten later issued the following statement:

"Following video review, it was determined Western Michigan's #18 started his jump from an established out-of-bounds position (left foot) and made contact with the ball with one second remaining on the clock. As shown in the provided video of what was viewed during the replay process, a side-by-side view of the play and the game clock, using a direct shot of the game clock in the stadium, in the stadium, was used to determined the final ruling. Eighty-five minutes prior to the game, all broadcast cameras used for the replay system, including the camera on the game clock, are synced using a strobe system to ensure all cameras are aligned.

"Per NCAA Football rule 4-2-3-1, 'A ball not in player control, other than a kick that scores a field goal, is out of bounds when it touches the ground, a player, a game official or anything else that is out-of-bound, or that is on or outside the boundary line' and thus the clock is stopped."

NBC addressed the issue during halftime of the its broadcast of the Washington-Washington State game Sunday, with host John Fanta noting that the clock on the screen is not the official clock. Officials are responsible for tracking the official clock with the conference of the home team.

Regardless, Pereira says officials are taught to side with the clock that America is seeing over something internally.

"Here's the key, and here's where it got lost: The replay officials have been told that if there is a discrepancy, you use the television footage," Pereira told Fox colleague Joel Klatt on a podcast. "Do not use your footage in the Command Center. Use the footage that 2 million people are watching, not the one that's three [people watching]."

With 9 seconds left in the game on Saturday, Sept. 5, U-M quarterback Bryce Underwood heaved a Hail Mary from midfield through the back of the end zone, apparently ending the game as a 12-7 WMU victory. The clocks on the TV broadcast – and the video boards at the stadium – showed no time left.

After a video review, however, officials determined the ball was touched by a formerly out-of-bounds WMU defender with 1 second left and restored that on the clock, allowing another play. Underwood than connected with receiver JJ Buchanan on a second Hail Mary for a 13-12 win.

The Big Ten later issued the following statement:

"Following video review, it was determined Western Michigan's #18 started his jump from an established out-of-bounds position (left foot) and made contact with the ball with one second remaining on the clock. As shown in the provided video of what was viewed during the replay process, a side-by-side view of the play and the game clock, using a direct shot of the game clock in the stadium, in the stadium, was used to determined the final ruling. Eighty-five minutes prior to the game, all broadcast cameras used for the replay system, including the camera on the game clock, are synced using a strobe system to ensure all cameras are aligned.

"Per NCAA Football rule 4-2-3-1, 'A ball not in player control, other than a kick that scores a field goal, is out of bounds when it touches the ground, a player, a game official or anything else that is out-of-bound, or that is on or outside the boundary line' and thus the clock is stopped."

See Hail Mary play that saved Michigan and sent Western Michigan home sick

NBC addressed the issue during halftime of the its broadcast of the Washington-Washington State game Sunday, with host John Fanta noting that the clock on the screen is not the official clock. Officials are responsible for tracking the official clock with the conference of the home team.

Regardless, Pereira says officials are taught to side with the clock that America is seeing over something internally.

"Here's the key, and here's where it got lost: The replay officials have been told that if there is a discrepancy, you use the television footage," Pereira told Fox colleague Joel Klatt on a podcast. "Do not use your footage in the Command Center. Use the footage that 2 million people are watching, not the one that's three [people watching]."

articles.title: Projecting the Baltimore Ravens’ wide receiver rotation
articles.summary: Baltimore’s receiver rotation combines two established starters with four younger and versatile options
articles.body:
After months of waiting, Baltimore will play a meaningful regular-season game when they take on the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1. One position to watch is the revamped wide receiver group that could be among the most explosive in the NFL. Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman should dominate Baltimore's receiver snaps, but the remaining hierarchy is less settled.

Flowers will move throughout the formation and remain Lamar Jackson's primary target. Bateman should handle the largest share of outside routes and provide the offense with a vertical threat. After a strong training camp, rookie pass catcher Ja'Kobi Lane is the leading candidate for the third role. His 6-foot-4 frame provides a larger target on third down and near the goal line.

Elijah Sarratt can also play inside or outside and should find key snaps behind Lane. His physical style could earn him an early role on running downs and possession routes. Devontez Walker remains one of Baltimore's fastest receivers. His opportunities may come on designed vertical routes rather than a large weekly snap count.

LaJohntay Wester will contribute as a returner and could receive manufactured touches on screens, jet sweeps, and quick passes. Flowers and Bateman could each play more than 70% of the snaps. Lane should begin in the 35% to 50% range, with Sarratt, Walker and Wester dividing the remaining opportunities.

Baltimore does not need one young receiver to claim every available snap. Declan Doyle can use their different traits to create a situational rotation.

articles.title: Colts defense given top-10 ceiling entering 2026 season
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts defense was given a top-10 ceiling for 2026 after injuries prevented several key players from staying on the field last season.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts enter the 2026 season with some uncertainty surrounding their offense, but the potential on the other side of the ball is drawing attention.

The Ringer's Sheil Kapadia wrote in his Sept. 7 AFC South preview that Indianapolis could field "one of the NFL's most improved units" this season, adding that the defense has a top-10 ceiling if its key veterans remain healthier and its rookie class contributes.

"Corner Sauce Gardner was on the field for just four games last year after the big in-season trade. Cornerback Charvarius Ward played in just seven games. And defensive tackle DeForest Buckner was healthy for only 10," Kapadia wrote.

The Ringer's Anthony Dabbundo ranked Indianapolis 16th among NFL defenses in a separate preseason ranking on Sept. 2. He praised a secondary featuring Gardner, Ward and Camryn Bynum but identified the pass rush and young linebacker corps as important variables.

Dabbundo specifically pointed to Laiatu Latu's development as a possible ceiling-raiser. Indianapolis will also lean heavily on its young defenders, with 2026 draft picks CJ Allen, Bryce Boettcher, and A.J. Haulcy all projected for prominent roles.

If that youth develops quickly and Indianapolis gets more games from its noteworthy stars, the defense could become one of the roster's biggest strengths.

articles.title: Michael Penix: I'm close to 100 percent, but I'm not there yet
articles.summary: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski named Tua Tagovailoa the team's starting quarterback for the first game of the season on Monday and that decision was not...
articles.body:
Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski named Tua Tagovailoa the team's starting quarterback for the first game of the season on Monday and that decision was not made over any objection from Michael Penix.

Penix was cleared for 11-on-11 work near the end of August and the quarterback said on Monday that he told Stefanski that he still does not feel like he's fully recovered from last year's torn ACL. Penix, who will be inactive in Week 1, said that he wants "to be stronger" and that it isn't fair to the team to try to go out there until "there's no doubt in my mind that I trust my knee."

"I just told him I'm not where I want to be right now ," Penix said, via the team's website. "And I want to be able to be 100 percent so I can help the team win football games. And I'm really close. Really close."

Penix has recovered from two other torn ACLs and said that he feels like he tried to come back too soon in the past, so he wants to avoid a similar situation this time. That opens the door for Tagovailoa to seize the job more convincingly than he did this summer, but that's a risk that Penix appears to be more comfortable with than any having to do with his health.

articles.title: Future of Liverpool’s most important player confirmed after major transfer news emerges
articles.summary: Liverpool finally got their first win of the Premier League season under their belt on Friday. Andoni Iraola led his men to a 2-0 win against the recently pr...
articles.body:
Liverpool finally got their first win of the Premier League season under their belt on Friday.

Andoni Iraola led his men to a 2-0 win against the recently promoted Ipswich and, while Liverpool should have easily beaten them, the fact that they did it with such ease was a nice surprise.

Recently, the Anfield outfit looked like they were lacking identity but, after Friday's win, it finally feels like the Reds could be getting back to their best.

Obviously, it's still early days so things could definitely change but, as long as Iraola continues to drill his style of football into his first-team squad, they'll eventually come out on top.

However, even though the transfer window has just slammed shut, talk of the Reds' next dealings are already being shared and now, the future of their most important player is under scrutiny.

Cody Gakpo could be on his way out of Liverpool as they're still eyeing a move for Ismaila Sarr

One of the main priorities that Liverpool had during the 2026-27 summer transfer window was to find a replacement for Mohamed Salah , or, at the very least, strengthen their attack.

By doing this, they'd have been able to work on the mistakes that they made last term and would be able to try and improve their ranking in the Premier League.

Indeed, Liverpool did end up adding Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz to their ranks but, alongside players joining them, many were linked with moves away.

And, up until the final hours of deadline day, nobody actually knew what Liverpool's squad was going to look like so, it's hardly surprising to see decisions potentially already being made about the upcoming January transfer window.

In fact, a recent update from Football Insider seems to have all but confirmed the future of Cody Gakpo .

"Liverpool will consider making another move to sign Ismaila Sarr in January after failing to agree a deal before the summer deadline, sources have told Football Insider," they shared .

"Sarr was a target for the Reds throughout the transfer window after impressing for Crystal Palace over the last few seasons.

"Andoni Iraola wanted to add quality and depth to his attacking ranks following Mo Salah's departure.

"Bradley Barcola arrived in a move worth £120million before the deadline, and they remained hot on the trail of Sarr but failed to get a deal done.

"Sarr still wants to join Liverpool and he will stay on their radar in the months to come."

Liverpool cannot replace Cody Gakpo with Ismaila Sarr anymore

When Sarr was being linked with a Liverpool transfer , there was a mixed reaction from fans.

However, the common consensus was that as long as the price was right, the deal could be good for Liverpool as, not only is he a natural right-winger but he's also got plenty of Premier League experience under his belt.

In the end, Crystal Palace demanded too much money for his transfer which led to Liverpool dropping out of the race for the Senegal international and resulted in them pulling the plug on Gakpo's move to Manchester City or Tottenham.

At the time, Liverpool turning down around €100 million for the Dutchman was seen as insane to some fans but, now that he's here. they'll probably be glad he's stayed put.

Since the start of the 2026-27 season, he's easily been Liverpool's most important player as he's even managed to contribute to more goals than he's played so far.

Of course, we don't know how well Sarr is going to do upon his return from action but, with the current run of form Gakpo is in, there's no way that Iraola should even be considering the exit of Gakpo under any circumstances.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Team USA Dealt Unwanted Blow After Italy Thriller
articles.summary: ​Team USA women's basketball picked up a narrow 55-52 victory over Italy on Sunday in its FIBA World Cup matchup. ​​The win was nowhere near as commanding as...
articles.body:
​Team USA women's basketball picked up a narrow 55-52 victory over Italy on Sunday in its FIBA World Cup matchup.

​​The win was nowhere near as commanding as the Americans' previous victory over China, as Italy gave Team USA a major scare throughout the contest.

​Team "USA's 55 points tonight mark its lowest-scoring World Cup game since 1971," noted ESPN's Alexa Philippou.

​USA head coach Kara Lawson acknowledged that the Americans won't always be at their best following the narrow victory.

​ "Every single one of those wins came hard. … and we understand that," said USA coach Kara Lawson, whose team advanced to the quarterfinals with the victory.

"You have to have great respect for who you play; you have to prepare in a way to win. And so, it's supposed to be challenging, and we're supposed to have moments where we're not at our best."

​ Team USA Survives Italy's Second-Half Push

The Americans jumped out to a commanding start, taking a 23-8 lead. However, what looked like a comfortable victory quickly turned into a battle as Italy stormed back to cut the deficit to 30-24 by halftime.

Italy continued applying pressure, putting together an 11-2 run in the third quarter and showing no quit. However, the fourth quarter proved to be the difference for the Americans.

​After trailing 50-48, Team USA went on a 7-0 run in the fourth quarter, thanks in part to Breanna Stewart, who missed her first eight shots before eventually hitting a shot with three minutes to go to give Team USA some life.

Las Vegas Aces star Jackie Young led Team USA with 10 points, but it was her teammate Chelsea Gray who stole the show.

After connecting on a layup and hitting some free throws, Gray knocked down the biggest shot of the game, hitting a clutch jumper with 1:07 remaining that would seal the win for the United States.

​ ​"I thought that the late charge Chelsea took was a big momentum-changing play," Lawson said. "It was an incredible winning play by Gray there."

​It was an ugly performance for Team USA, which shot just 29% from the field. The Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark hit a new career low with zero field goals. However, the Americans ultimately did enough to escape with the victory.

​ Despite picking up the win, Paige Bueckers revealed that the team still has plenty to learn from the game.

​ "Definitely I think there are learning experiences and growth from every single game," she told reporters on Sunday. "But to be challenged like this early for our group, I think it's great for us in the long run."

Italy had previously lost to the Americans by as much as 34 points in a tournament qualifier in March. Team USA has won 32 straight World Cup games, dating back to the loss in 2006 against ​Russia.

​The United States is now 2-0 in Group D play and will look to continue its winning ways against the Czech Republic in its final group-stage game.

articles.title: Even after 71-3 victory, Collin Klein wants more from Kansas State
articles.summary: After a 71-3 win, Collin Klein isn't celebrating. Here's why the Kansas State coach is focused on fixing mistakes and preparing for Washington State.
articles.body:
MANHATTAN — In the aftermath of a 71-3 victory to open the season , Kansas State coach Collin Klein hasn't allowed himself to get too high. In fact, the first-year coach is quick to point out the mistakes the Wildcats made and what they need to do to improve.

There is no room for fumbling the ball, nor can the Wildcats kick the ball out of bounds twice on kickoffs. It doesn't matter if they held Nicholls to 30 yards passing or beat them by 68 points .

"I just try to be as fact-based as possible," Klein said. "It's easy to let emotion flower things up when they're good and overcloud things when they're not. I think walking in the middle of 'Hey, these are the facts, this is actually what happened, and I'm going to shoot you straight' and that there's good and bad always with that. As long as that's our focus, I think it'll create a consistent process and approach."

It hasn't been all sunshine and rainbows from the coach since his first career win . Immediately after the game, he said the Wildcats didn't win the turnover margin, while also noting other small things that needed to be cleaned up.

Kansas State football returns for 2026-27 season vs Nicholls State

During his Monday presser ahead of the Wildcats' 11 a.m. game on Saturday, Sept. 12, against Washington State (0-1) at Bill Snyder Family Stadium, he even pointed the finger at himself and his staff for the mistakes they made.

"The little things didn't catch us, but when we make mistakes, we have to get them shored up," Klein said. "We have a big week ahead of us."

We continue to learn more about Klein's approach as a young, first-year head coach. Longtime reporters in the room laughed and gave Klein a hard time, saying he sounded exactly like the legendary Bill Snyder, who Klein played for and coached under. It's how Klein is wired.

He was locked in from start to finish. Up 57-3 heading into the fourth quarter, Bill Snyder Family Stadium debuted its new light show, which included pyrotechnics. Klein said he didn't really notice because he was looking at his playsheet and trying to plan the next play. He did notice, however, that the Wildcats got a holding penalty on the first play after it. That, too, needs to be cleaned up.

After the game, Klein got splashed with water by his team in the locker room to celebrate his first victory, but that's when the party stopped for him. There was no time to reflect on what it meant to be back in Bill Snyder Family Stadium while living out his dream.

The coach said he flipped the page to Washington State shortly after, knowing the Cougars had a game the following afternoon and they would be a much more formidable opponent.

"The mentality that has helped me, the team and the program truly is that we take care of the next thing that's right in front of you," Klein said. "That's the mindset. I'm proud of our players for the good start, but I told the team this morning that it's 0-0 and we gotta go."

Wyatt D. Wheeler covers Kansas State athletics for the USA TODAY Network and Topeka Capital-Journal. You can follow him on X at @WyattWheeler_ , contact him at 417-371-6987 or email him at wwheeler@usatodayco.com
