articles.title: Kyle Shanahan explains how 49ers reacted to devastating offseason news
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers saw one of their rivals get one of the greatest players in NFL history back for 2026, and here's how they reacted to the news.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have watched their NFC West rivals, the Los Angeles Rams , add several talented players to their roster this offseason, including defensive lineman Aaron Donald , who unretired after two seasons to play in 2026.

Donald is considered one of the greatest football players in the sport's history. In 154 games, he's recorded 543 tackles, 260 quarterback hits, 111 sacks, 24 forced fumbles, 21 passes defensed and seven fumble recoveries. He also made 10 Pro Bowls, eight All-Pro teams, won Defensive Player of the Year three times, won Defensive Rookie of the Year once and won a Super Bowl.

Now that he's returning to the game, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan revealed his team's reaction to both the day that he called it a career and his comeback.

"I remember when he retired, I didn't see the alerts and stuff, but I heard people yelling down the hallway, cheering. I was like, 'what the heck is going on?' And then I got it on my phone, and it was probably the most we've celebrated in the offseason ever," Shanahan told reporters in Australia this week. "And then it was the exact opposite this year. I wasn't crushed on the Sunday that he decided because I decided a month ago it was happening. So, I prepared for that the right way, and it is what it is. He's a hell of a player, and we'll have our work cut out for him."

Donald still appears to be in incredible shape, and he doesn't seem like the type of player to just lose his ability, even at 35 years old, but we won't know until we see him in a game, which will likely be this week against San Francisco .

The 49ers should be concerned, considering their latest depth chart still has Connor Colby at left guard, which didn't go well at all in 2025 or at any point during training camp this year. Donald could dominate the middle of the line with Braden Fiske and Kobie Turner , while newcomer Myles Garrett attacks the edge opposite Byron Young .

articles.title: Drew Brees replaces Maxx Crosby on SiriusXM’s ‘Let’s Go!’
articles.summary: The media renaissance of Drew Brees continues unabated. Not only will the former New Orleans Saints quarterback embark on his first full season in the booth...
articles.body:
The media renaissance of Drew Brees continues unabated.

Not only will the former New Orleans Saints quarterback embark on his first full season in the booth alongside Adam Amin for the NFL on Fox, but the 47-year-old will also co-host SiriusXM's Let's Go! alongside Matthew Stafford, Jim Gray and Peter King, effectively replacing Las Vegas Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby

It remains unclear why Crosby is departing as a co-host, though he continues to grow his media footprint, co-hosting The Rush Podcast with Brogan Roback and Darien Terrell. As does Brees, who spent much of the past year publicly guaranteeing his own greatness well before he'd actually done the work to substantiate it. Before joining Fox to replace Mark Sanchez, Brees hadn't called an NFL game since his tenure at NBC ended somewhat unceremoniously, though he's insisted all along it was his own decision rather than the network's.

Brees joined NBC right after retiring in 2021, with expectations he'd eventually take over Cris Collinsworth's Sunday Night Football seat. Instead, he called Notre Dame games on Saturdays and worked the Football Night in America studio show. NBC put him on a playoff game that January, Raiders-Bengals on Wild Card weekend, and it didn't go particularly well.

In his eventual return to the broadcast booth after four years away, Brees avoided the interminable dead air that had sunk his earlier stint, showed a real and natural feel for the rhythm of a broadcast alongside partner Adam Amin, and displayed the kind of football fluency that comes from having actually played the position at an elite level, even if he still fell measurably short of the top-three analyst status he'd spent years publicly guaranteeing he'd inevitably reach.

Also joining SiriusXM this season are New York Giants defensive tackle Shelby Harris, New York Jets linebacker Demario Davis, and free agent wide receiver Brandin Cooks, who will rotate as hosts alongside Carolina Panthers long snapper J.J. Jansen and Los Angeles Chargers fullback Alec Ingold on the weekly program The Players' Point, billed as the only radio show hosted by active NFL players. Adam Thielen, who retired earlier this year following a 13-year NFL career, has likewise signed on as a SiriusXM host. He'll be heard Tuesdays from 10 a.m. to noon ET on Airing It Out alongside Bob Papa.
